title: Doc-truth gate trips on prose that DESCRIBES its own detectors
description:
WHAT: verify_doc_consistency.py scan_publication() flags any markdown pairing _FLIP (publication|visibility flip|going public|...) with _STUCK (pending|blocked|deferred|awaiting|...) within 60 chars. It cannot distinguish ASSERTING that publication is pending from DESCRIBING a detector that looks for that assertion.

WHY: measured 2026-08-12, cost a full ~12min check.sh cycle. README gained a table row naming selftest_doc_consistency injections, one of which is literally "publication described as pending". The scanner matched its own trigger phrase inside documentation OF ITSELF and failed the build at README.md:240, before check.sh ever reached the drift-guard step it was running to validate. Worked around by rewording to "stale pre-flip visibility claim" — accurate, and dodges the alternation.

The bite is that documenting a detector is now a build hazard: the more precisely you name what a gate catches, the likelier you trip it. The next agent to document these injections will hit this and may reach for the wrong fix.

NOT-A-BUG READING (record before choosing): fail-closed keyword scanning prefers a false positive to a miss, and the workaround is one reword. Weakening the pattern to reduce false positives risks the real misses this gate exists to catch. Doing nothing is defensible IF the hazard is written down.

ACCEPTANCE — exactly one of:
 (a) an explicit per-line opt-out marker (e.g. a trailing <!-- doc-truth: describes-detector --> ) honoured by scan_publication, WITH a known-bad injection proving an UNMARKED assertion still trips RED (the opt-out must not become a blanket bypass); or
 (b) decision recorded as WONTFIX in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md naming this incident, the 60-char window, and the reword workaround, so the next agent does not weaken the pattern to escape it.
Either way: the _FLIP/_STUCK alternations must NOT be narrowed to dodge this — that trades a real detection for a cosmetic one.

title: check.sh step count is advertised in README but NOT drift-guarded
description:
WHAT: README.md:49 advertises "<N> ordered steps" for check.sh. verify_injection_count.py guards the injection total and the suite count in that SAME SENTENCE, but not the step count. Nothing enforces it.

WHY: measured 2026-08-13, and the orchestrator got it wrong IMMEDIATELY after building the guard. README was written as 58 from a subagent report; that subagent run ABORTED at the drift guard, so it counted 58 before failing. The passing run emits 59. The wrong number was committed and PUSHED PUBLIC, surviving a fully green check.sh (exit 0) because the guard does not look at it.

This is bd-1sd.4 recurring one field to the left. The lesson of .4 was that a hand-maintained count adjacent to enforced ones reads exactly like an enforced one -- to readers AND to the person editing it. Two of the three numbers in that sentence are derived from runtime receipts; the third is folklore.

ACCEPTANCE:
- check.sh emits a machine-readable receipt for its own step count on the success path (same contract as INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>), and verify_injection_count.py (or a sibling) compares it to every "<N> ordered steps" claim in README.md.
- Anti-vacuous, per the existing contract: a MISSING step receipt is an ERROR, never a silent zero or a skip.
- Known-bad injection proving it bites: edit README step count by one -> check.sh RED with a message naming the file:line and both numbers. Add it to selftest_injection_count.sh and increment that suite INJECTIONS= receipt accordingly (the drift guard will then require the README injection total to move too -- that coupling is correct and is the point).
- Prove-it-bites meta-test: delete the new assertion -> selftest exits non-zero.

NOTE: counting is subtle -- 59 is `grep -c "check.sh: ok:"` on a PASSING run. Steps that fail early never emit ok:, which is exactly how 58 was produced. Define the receipt from what check.sh COUNTS as it runs, not from grepping its transcript afterwards.

title: ASHRAE captures marked redistribution:not-licensed are published in a PUBLIC repo
description:
WHAT: knowledge/corpus/public/src-ashrae-datacom.txt (11257 B) and src-ashrae-power-wp.txt (586 B) are committed to a PUBLIC GitHub repo while manifest.json records them as rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed".

WHY: retaining a capture for internal grounding and publishing it worldwide are different acts; the second IS redistribution, which the manifest itself says is not licensed. Two compounding factors, both discovered 2026-08-13:
 (1) ASHRAE published AI policy, verbatim: "ASHRAE prohibits the entry of content from any ASHRAE publication or related ASHRAE intellectual property (IP) into any AI tool... Additionally, creating derivative works of ASHRAE IP using AI is also prohibited without express written permission." This repo was AI-built end to end.
 (2) Three ASHRAE PDFs were already purged from HEAD AND git history on 2026-08-12 for the same class of concern. These .txt captures survived that purge.

Not alarmist: the manifest hygiene is GOOD -- rights were recorded honestly rather than assumed permissive, and the retention_basis already states the purpose is "so the claim can be re-verified at source". That stated purpose is fully served without shipping any captured text.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Replace both files with citation-only rows carrying {url, title, publisher, fetched_at, rights, redistribution} and ZERO publisher-derived prose/body text.
- grep for ASHRAE-derived narrative text under knowledge/corpus/public/ returns nothing beyond bibliographic fields.
- manifest.json no longer contains any entry whose redistribution="not-licensed" while its path is inside the published tree -- add a CHECK for exactly that invariant to scripts/ and wire it into check.sh with || fail.
- Known-bad injection proving it bites: plant a manifest entry with redistribution="not-licensed" pointing at a public path -> check.sh RED with the file named. Meta-test: delete the assertion -> selftest exits non-zero.
- Decide and RECORD whether git-history purge is needed for these two files or whether HEAD removal suffices (they are small public-page captures, not standard body text -- the answer may legitimately be HEAD-only; state the reasoning either way).

NOTE: this invariant generalises beyond ASHRAE. Any future corpus artifact whose recorded redistribution is not licensed must never live inside the published tree. The gate should enforce the general rule, not an ASHRAE special case.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: DONE (2026-08-14).

REMOVED FROM HEAD: knowledge/corpus/public/src-ashrae-datacom.txt (11257 B), src-ashrae-power-wp.txt (586 B) via git rm. Neither file was opened, read, quoted or summarised at any point -- ASHRAE's AI policy prohibits entering ASHRAE IP into any AI tool, and removing a file does not require reading it.

RETAINED: capture="citation-only" rows in manifest.json (now schema cdcp.corpus.manifest.v2) carrying exactly {id, title, publisher, url, fetched_at, access, rights, redistribution, ai_ingestion, retention_basis} plus a removal audit trail (body_removed_at / body_removed_bead / body_removed_sha256_of_prior_capture). ZERO publisher-derived prose. path and bytes keys dropped. sources.toml ids and the topics.toml / standards_families.toml references remain valid -- the source records still exist, only the bodies are gone.

VERIFIED: no file under corpus/public/ carries ASHRAE-derived narrative. grep -ril ashrae returns manifest.json (bibliographic fields), src-tia-942-c-fotc.txt (3) and src-curriculum-map-local.txt (2); a count-only 600-char-window scan of those two for thermal-envelope markers (A1-A4, dew point, degC, RH) returned 0 -- they name the organisation, they do not reproduce its IP. validate_grounding.py PASS high_severity=0. tests/publishability-bar.sh 23 passed 0 failed.

GENERALISED, not instance-fixed. New enforcement target knowledge/corpus/rights-policy.toml (schema cdcp.corpus.rights-policy.v1) with 6 invariants and 6 [[known_bad]] fixtures so the gate can be PROVEN TO TRIP:
  CORPUS-R1 no record with redistribution != permitted may be capture=body-retained with a path inside the published tree
  CORPUS-R2 rights/redistribution/capture REQUIRED; missing or out-of-vocabulary = ERROR, never default-permissive
  CORPUS-R3 a record declaring third_party_figures may not be public-domain or redistribution=permitted
  CORPUS-R4 an R1 exception needs rights_review=OPEN + a bead + a non-empty reason; a bare exemption is a schema error
  CORPUS-R5 zero records scanned = ERROR; never vacuously green
  CORPUS-R6 ai_ingestion=PROHIBITED implies capture must be citation-only or not-vendored

The Rust gate is bead D4 and was NOT built here (not mine). rights-policy.toml is the artifact D4 enforces against. scripts/check.sh untouched. No new .py or .sh. Nothing committed.

CLASS RESIDUE, tracked not tolerated: the strict CORPUS-R1 reading implicates TEN more sources, not two -- every remaining public/ capture carries rights=publisher-retains-copyright, redistribution=not-licensed and is committed to the public tree. Not swept in this pass because scripts/validate_grounding.py consumes those bodies as its grounding corpus (601k chars, 804 items); removing them without a replacement grounding source takes the build red under four concurrently active agents. Each now carries rights_review=OPEN + rights_review_bead + rights_review_reason in manifest.json and is listed under [[open_violation]] in rights-policy.toml. Filed as bd-corpus-public-captures-not-licensed-class-kej.

GIT HISTORY PURGE: NOT NEEDED. HEAD removal suffices. Not performed (danger-list).
Evidence, all from regex counts that emit integers and never surface matched text:
 - Both entered in one commit, 5c98662, which IS on origin/main -- exposure was real, which is why HEAD removal was required.
 - src-ashrae-power-wp.txt contains ZERO ASHRAE content. Its url ends .pdf so fetch_public_corpus.py took its PDF branch and wrote OUR OWN stub "[PDF not extracted in-repo]" + url + title (stub marker count 1, 586 B, 10 lines). It was already a citation row wearing a .txt extension. Nothing to purge.
 - src-ashrae-datacom.txt is a bookstore/catalogue landing page: 342 lines but only ~10 sentences >=40 chars and 8 store-navigation markers; ZERO thermal-envelope markers and ZERO table/figure captions. No standards content, no tables, no thermal-guideline data.
 - Materially different from the 2026-08-12 purge, which removed three full ASHRAE TC 9.9 PUBLICATIONS -- actual technical content. Applying the same remedy to a catalogue page is cargo-culting the precedent, not reasoning from it.
 - Same bytes ASHRAE serves unauthenticated at that URL; no access control circumvented.
 - A rewrite would not achieve retraction: repo public since 2026-08-12, so force-pushing does not reach clones or forks and GitHub keeps unreferenced objects fetchable by SHA until GC. Near-zero actual retraction, real cost -- rewrites every commit since 5c98662 and forces a hard reset on four live agents.
COUNTERFACTUAL: had either file contained standards body text -- clause text, envelope tables, figure data -- the calculus inverts; volume would be irrelevant next to the AI-policy and derivative-works exposure, and this would have STOPPED and escalated to Josh for a supervised rewrite rather than performed one.

RECEIPT: docs/flywheel/PREPUBLISH-SCRUB-2026-08-14.md

title: DOE/FEMP Best Practices Guide embeds ASHRAE tables - NOT vendorable as-is
description:
WHAT: best-practice-guide-data-center-design.pdf (48pp, DOE/FEMP/LBNL/NREL) carries the standard US Government disclaimer, but REPRODUCES ASHRAE material under attribution:

 - "Source: Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments, ASHRAE" (x3)
 - "Source: Emergence and Expansion of Liquid Cooling in Mainstream Data Centers, ASHRAE" (x2)

WHY: two independent consequences.
 (1) RIGHTS: third-party material embedded in a US Government work does NOT become public domain (17 USC 105 covers the government-authored portions only). Vendoring this PDF into the PUBLIC repo would republish ASHRAE tables. Review round 2 flagged exactly this risk; it is now confirmed rather than suspected.
 (2) AI POLICY: ASHRAE prohibits entry of ASHRAE IP into any AI tool. The policy binds on CONTENT, not container -- reading Table 3-1 violates it regardless of the government wrapper. Table 3-1 is the A1-A4 thermal envelope data this project has been deliberately marking UNGROUNDED, so the guide is a side-door route to exactly the material that must stay ungrounded until a human reads it.

ACCEPTANCE:

title: Near-duplicate bank items are undetected; m14-q040/m14-q121 are one item twice
description:
WHAT: m14-q040 and m14-q121 are the SAME item with the key shuffled (B vs A) and distractors cosmetically reworded ("Replaces daily backups of VMs" vs "Replaces daily VM backups"; "Only tests a single breaker nameplate" vs "...in isolation forever"). Key text is identical verbatim. Exact-stem hashing over all 804 items finds ZERO duplicate groups, so no existing gate detects this class.

WHY: three compounding consequences.
 (1) ASSESSMENT INFLATION. cdcp_assemble samples every loaded item and BankItem has no status field, so one mock can draw both, scoring a single proposition twice and showing the learner the answer they just gave.
 (2) THE 804 COUNT IS UNTRUSTWORTHY. Duplication of unknown extent inflates the headline metric. Discovered while verifying commissioning coverage: 6 items match commissioning vocabulary, but 2 are this pair, 1 uses the word only inside a lighting distractor, and 1 uses "commission" as a verb meaning order a survey -- leaving ~2 substantive propositions, not 6.
 (3) PREREQUISITE FOR ANY GENERATION. Review round 3 warned that generated items form families with correlated flaws. Near-duplicate detection must exist BEFORE generation, or generation silently inflates a metric that already cannot be trusted.

Both items also exhibit the giveaway-distractor defect: "Replaces daily VM backups" and "Is optional marketing text with no technical meaning" are answerable by spotting absurdity rather than knowing what an IST is.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A near-duplicate detector over bank/items: normalised stem + normalised key-text similarity (not exact hash -- exact hashing demonstrably returns 0 here). Threshold recorded and justified; flags pairs above it.
- Wired into check.sh with || fail. Anti-vacuous: zero items scanned is an ERROR, not a pass.
- Known-bad injection: plant a cosmetically-reworded copy of an existing item -> check.sh RED naming both ids. Meta-test: delete the assertion -> selftest exits non-zero.
- Resolve m14-q040 / m14-q121: retire one, or differentiate them into genuinely distinct propositions. Record which and why.
- Report the bank-wide near-duplicate count so the true distinct-proposition number is known. Do NOT preserve 804 as a target.

NOTE: pairs with DIFFERENT correct letters are the dangerous subclass -- a reviewer eyeballing keys will not notice, because the letters differ.

title: EPIC B: Machine ledgers — evidence stops living in prose
description:
WHAT: adopt frankensim machine-ledger patterns so capability and golden claims are mechanically falsifiable.

WHY: `L3 External oracle | YES · wired` survived for months in a CHARTER table because a maturity claim in prose has no mechanical falsifier. P0 corrected the instance; B removes the class. Ships BEFORE C so that C-era claims cannot rot the same way.

## Success Criteria
Every capability claim names a test function and a review date that expires. Every golden names the semantic surfaces it depends on at pinned versions. check.sh fails on a stale row, a drifted surface, or a silent re-freeze.

title: EPIC C: Item status and assembly filter — the gate everything waits on
description:
WHAT: give BankItem a lifecycle status, restrict assembly to approved items, repair the content address, and close the correctness holes in assembly.

WHY: BankItem has no status field and cdcp_assemble samples every loaded item. Any content authored today lands in the same undifferentiated pool as the existing 804 — a pool that already contains an undetectable near-duplicate pair (m14-q040 / m14-q121) and 39 items for a module with no Learn surface. THE CURRICULUM DAG CANNOT START UNTIL C LANDS.

## Success Criteria
Assembly draws only approved items; bank_hash covers every semantically load-bearing field; near-duplicates are detected; the PRNG is portable and named; module 15 has a recorded decision.

title: EPIC D: Evidence spine — cdcp_evidence
description:
WHAT: build cdcp_evidence carrying frankensim Evidence<T> semantics — certificates that travel INSIDE values.

WHY: review round 3 killed the plant-model thesis because every omitted dependency becomes an invisible axiom. frankensim hit the same wall and solved it: attach the certificate to the value so it cannot fall off, and make composition conservative so a weak input cannot be laundered into a strong conclusion.

## Success Criteria
ModelEvidence composition intersects validity domains, adds discrepancy, rounds enclosures outward; in_domain propagates false; an approved item making a normative claim with no resolvable evidence row is RED.

title: EPIC E: Public data corpus — cdcp_data
description:
WHAT: licence-gated, content-addressed loader for vendored public-domain snapshots. No network I/O; snapshots pinned at build time.

WHY: PD-GOV datasets (NOAA, USGS, FEMA, EPA eGRID, EIA, OSHA/eCFR) are external, authoritative about physical reality, versioned, and freely redistributable AND AI-ingestible — the one tier with no restriction. They are the substrate for the first real external oracle (F).

## Success Criteria
The loader REFUSES an artifact whose .meta.toml lacks a licence line; zero artifacts scanned is an ERROR; content.lock covers data artifacts.

title: EPIC F: Computation and the first real external oracle
description:
WHAT: cdcp_site and cdcp_metrics, plus the differential harness that compares computed values against published references from sources we do not control.

WHY: this is the ONLY route to an honest L3. Three review rounds established that citation integrity is not validation and deduction from an authored model is not truth. Computing from measured public data and disagreeing with published analysis is falsifiable in the way an oracle must be.

## Success Criteria
Computed free-cooling hours / seismic / grid carbon match published reference values for known locations, or the build is RED. MMS-style manufactured cases with closed-form answers cover every computed quantity.

title: EPIC G: Typed assessment — cdcp_assess
description:
WHAT: assessment kinds beyond the 4-letter MCQ — multi-select, ordering, numeric-range, topology-selection, procedural-sequence.

WHY: ChoiceLetter is four letters, BankItem stores one correct letter, and cdcp_assemble hard-codes four choices. Without G, every computed or structured scenario flattens back into A-D and we have built a better answer-key generator inside the same recognition interface.

## Success Criteria
Integer/rational arithmetic only; identical fixtures pass native and WASM; existing 804 items migrate to an explicit kind without changing their grades.

title: EPIC I: Scheduling — cdcp_schedule
description:
WHAT: pure scheduler with injected time, versioned state, migration rules, reference fixtures; compiled to WASM; removes the duplicated JS scheduling law.

WHY: web/assets/js/srs.js is a 1d/3d ladder capped at 3 days (INTERVAL_STEPS=[1,3]) that was called SRS. P0 corrected the claim. I either earns the name by adopting a versioned reference implementation with conformance fixtures, or the product keeps calling it short-interval review permanently.

## Success Criteria
Scheduling law exists once, in Rust, with injected time; JS consumes it via WASM; conformance fixtures pin the intervals.

title: EPIC J: PX — plant model falsification experiment (GATED)
description:
WHAT: pre-registered falsification experiment for a power-first finite-state service-availability model, OUTSIDE the production bank.

WHY: review round 3 REJECTED the plant-model thesis as the same category error as v1 in more sophisticated form. It survives only as an experiment with kill conditions written BEFORE it runs. frankensim fs-convection states the boundary in one line: "Formula implementation can be numerically verified; physical prediction quality cannot."

## Success Criteria
Kill conditions pre-registered and honoured. Says "service-preserving under the model", never "safe" — OSHA Subpart S and NFPA 70E are the authorities on safe. Out-of-scope queries ABSTAIN via ValidityDomain rather than answering confidently.

title: EPIC K: Owner-engineer scenario capstone
description:
WHAT: the assessment that measures something an interviewer would recognise — land closed, produce the proposal: what to order, when, to what standard, commissioned how.

WHY: 804 four-option MCQs cannot carry an operational-competence claim. The knowledge graph already holds 41 Decision nodes and a live worked example with real dates.

## Success Criteria
At least one scenario is scored deterministically by cdcp_assess against data from cdcp_site/cdcp_metrics, with the graders reproducible native and WASM.

title: EPIC L: Attempt-event capture (NO psychometrics yet)
description:
WHAT: record item_version, bank_hash, learner_pseudonym, mode, exposure_count, chosen_option, correctness, latency, timestamp, prior_attempts.

WHY: item difficulty and discrimination are sample-dependent and unreliable at small N. Round 2 was explicit: do not build cdcp_stats before there is data. Capture first, analyse never-until-there-is-enough.

## Success Criteria
Local-first schema with explicit opt-in export; NO difficulty/discrimination computation ships in this epic; a minimum-N warning is designed in from the start.

title: EPIC M: Distribution — publish the corpus and the graph
description:
WHAT: publish the licence-audited public data corpus and the DC lifecycle knowledge graph as standalone contributions.

WHY: both are useful independently of whether the study tool is finished. The graph holds 1,221 nodes / 1,587 edges including 125 contradicts edges mapping where authorities genuinely disagree — material that does not exist elsewhere in public form.

## Success Criteria
Every published artifact carries a verified licence line; nothing with redistribution != permitted is in the published tree; the ASHRAE-capture contradiction (bd-ashrae-redistribution-contradiction-p5n) is resolved first.

title: B1: capability-maturity.toml with enforced staleness
description:
WHAT: a machine ledger of capability claims. Each row: id, title, level, owner, last_review, crates[], evidence[] where every evidence entry is {kind: contract|test, ref: <path or module::test_fn>}. Global staleness_days = 90.

WHY: CHARTER asserted `L3 External oracle | YES · wired` for months on internal-only evidence, because a maturity claim in a prose table has no mechanical falsifier. P0 fixed the instance. This removes the class: a claim that names a test and expires cannot quietly stay wrong. Pattern source: frankensim capability-maturity.json (schema frankensim-capability-maturity-v1, 15 capabilities, staleness_days 90).

## Acceptance Criteria
- registries/capability-maturity.toml exists; every row carries level, owner, last_review, and >=1 evidence ref.
- Every evidence ref of kind=test RESOLVES to a real test function; a dangling ref is RED.
- A row whose last_review is older than staleness_days is RED, naming the row and its age.
- Anti-vacuous: zero capability rows scanned is an ERROR, not a pass.
- Wired into scripts/check.sh with || fail.
- Known-bad injection: (a) point an evidence ref at a nonexistent test -> RED; (b) backdate a last_review past the window -> RED.
- Meta-test: delete either assertion -> the selftest exits non-zero.
- The L3 row is present and records level=NO for factual-content external oracle, with its evidence ref pointing at the CHARTER 5a text and the P0 commit.

title: B2: goldens-couplings.toml — close the silent re-freeze hole
description:
WHAT: a registry coupling every golden/replay hash to the upstream SEMANTIC SURFACES it depends on, at pinned version constants, each with a written justification.

WHY: LIVE DEFECT. We have byte-exact goldens and no coupling registry. The UPDATE_GOLDENS path is a silent escape hatch: change grader semantics, regenerate goldens, gate stays green, and NOTHING records that a semantic surface moved. Pattern source: frankensim golden-couplings.json (138 surfaces / 25 goldens) whose note states the rule exactly -- "an upstream semantic change must point at every downstream golden to re-freeze deliberately, never silently."

## Acceptance Criteria
- registries/goldens-couplings.toml lists each golden with: file, const, depends_on (surface=version pairs), justification (non-empty string; empty justification is a schema ERROR).
- Each named surface declares a version const IN SOURCE; the checker fails when a source const drifts from the registry.
- The checker fails when a golden pin drifts from its surface row.
- Surfaces to register at minimum: bank item schema, GradeReport shape, canonical_json rules, bank_hash payload.
- Anti-vacuous: zero goldens or zero surfaces scanned is an ERROR.
- Wired into check.sh with || fail.
- Known-bad injection: bump a source version const without updating the registry -> RED naming both. Meta-test: delete the assertion -> selftest non-zero.
- UPDATE_GOLDENS regeneration MUST fail unless every affected golden row is re-justified in the same change.

title: B3: generalise doc-truth beyond milestone tables
description:
WHAT: extend verify_doc_consistency.py from milestone-status parsing to a doc-facts inventory: load-bearing prose claims tied to the artifacts that substantiate them.

WHY: the current gate checks milestone status across three files and publication truth over 95 markdown files. It caught a real M10 contradiction. But every OTHER load-bearing claim in the docs is unguarded -- exactly how the L3 claim survived. Pattern source: frankensim doc-facts-inventory.json (156 manifests / 156 contracts / 676 integration tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- An inventory maps each load-bearing doc claim class to the artifact that substantiates it (test, registry row, or generated ledger).
- A claim with no resolvable substantiating artifact is RED with file:line.
- Excluding a file requires a REASON STRING; an exclusion without a reason is a schema ERROR.
- Anti-vacuous: zero claims scanned is an ERROR.
- Complements, does not replace, the existing claims-lint (registries/claims_lint.toml).
- Known-bad injection + meta-test as per house standard.
- Must not regress: the existing milestone-agreement and publication-truth checks still trip on their planted specimens.

title: C1: BankItem status + assembly restricted to approved
description:
WHAT: add `status: draft | approved | retired` to BankItem; cdcp_assemble samples APPROVED ONLY.

WHY: THE blocking prerequisite for the entire curriculum DAG. BankItem has no status field and cdcp_assemble samples every loaded item (crates/cdcp_assemble/src/lib.rs sample_item_ids). Any content authored today lands in the same undifferentiated pool as the 804 -- a pool that already contains an undetectable near-duplicate pair and 39 items for a module with no Learn surface. Until C1 lands, nothing generated or written can be safely added.

## Acceptance Criteria
- BankItem carries status with an explicit default; unknown values are a load ERROR, not a silent default.
- cdcp_assemble draws only status=approved. A draft or retired item in the pool must NEVER appear in an assembled exam.
- Existing 804 items receive an explicit migration status (recorded decision: which value and why).
- Anti-vacuous: an assembly whose approved pool is EMPTY is an ERROR, not an empty exam.
- Known-bad injection: plant a draft item that would otherwise be sampled at a fixed seed -> assert it is absent from the assembled set; plant a retired item -> same. Meta-test: delete the filter -> selftest RED.
- Goldens: assembling at seed 42 before and after the filter must differ ONLY by the excluded items; the diff is recorded in the bead comment.
close_reason: C1 shipped ec5e3f6. ItemStatus{Draft,Approved,Retired} on BankItem, default=Draft (the status that cannot reach a learner); all 804 items explicitly approved. THREE selection paths filtered, including the max_per_module relaxation fallback that re-read bank.items.values() and is the leak a naive filter misses. Controller-verified: cargo test -p cdcp_assemble exit 0, 29 tests; empty_approved_pool_is_an_error_not_an_empty_exam present. Meta-test at authoring: filter deleted -> exit 101, 6 of 9 RED; restored -> 0. Graded: acceptance fully met.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
C1 IMPLEMENTED (not closed — orchestrator verifies/commits).

MIGRATION DECISION (804 items): default = draft; all 804 explicitly written `status = "approved"`.
Reasoning: the default must be the status that CANNOT reach a learner, or forgetting the field
reproduces the exact defect C1 exists to close (default=approved would auto-publish anything
authored). The 804 are approved because they ARE the shipped pool today (goldens, coverage,
grounding, orphan gates all green over them); downgrading them would empty the approved pool and
regress the product. C3 (near-duplicate pair) and C5 (module-15) are NOT pre-empted — those beads
flip specific items to retired/draft.

SEED-42 DIFF: EMPTY. Live Rust assembly at seed 42, computed on a clean HEAD worktree (pre-change,
pre-migration) and on the working tree (post-change), is identical in BOTH presentation order and
set; pool 804 -> 804 eligible. Zero items excluded, therefore zero difference.
Separate pre-existing observation: the live Rust seed-42 assembly does NOT equal
goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json (that fixture came from scripts/sample_mock.py / MT19937 —
documented in the crate header). True before and after this tick.

KNOWN-BAD + META-TEST (Rust, per mid-tick substrate-law correction — no new .sh/.py):
crates/cdcp_assemble/tests/status_filter.rs, 9 tests + 3 new cdcp_bank unit tests.
  filter deleted  -> cargo test -p cdcp_assemble exit 101 (6/9 RED)
  filter restored -> exit 0 (9/9 green)

bank_hash UNCHANGED (e8281757...); hash_payload deliberately untouched (C2, blocked on B2).

BLOCKER FOR VERIFICATION (NOT C1): check.sh exits 2 at step 4, cdcp_registry_check —
"docs/PLAN-A-TO-Z.md: load-bearing phrase class 'grade-exact' matched but file lacks markers for
[claim-grade-byte-exact]". Reproduced on a clean HEAD worktree, so it predates this tick (landed
with 8ef5e7b). Every other check.sh step was run individually and passes.

title: C2: bank_hash omits load-bearing fields
description:
WHAT: extend BankItem::hash_payload() to cover every semantically load-bearing field.

WHY: hash_payload() currently covers id, module, stem, choices, correct, explanation, topic_ids (crates/cdcp_bank/src/lib.rs ~L153). It OMITS objective_ids, citation ids, and status. The bank is described as content-addressed; adding evidence or flipping an item to retired would NOT change the hash. A content address that ignores load-bearing content is not a content address.

## Acceptance Criteria
- hash_payload covers: objective_ids, citation/evidence ids, status, plus existing fields.
- Schema version bumped; the change is registered as a SEMANTIC SURFACE in goldens-couplings (B2) so every dependent golden re-freezes deliberately with a justification.
- Known-bad injection: change ONLY objective_ids on one item -> bank_hash must change. Change ONLY status -> bank_hash must change. Meta-test: revert either field from the payload -> selftest RED.
- Unknown-field policy stated explicitly (reject vs ignore) and tested.
- All existing goldens re-frozen in ONE commit with a written justification naming this bead.

title: C4: StdRng is documented non-portable but called frozen
description:
WHAT: replace or pin the assembly PRNG with a portable, explicitly-named algorithm and a specified shuffle/sampling procedure.

WHY: crates/cdcp_assemble/src/lib.rs documents StdRng as freezing the algorithm ("currently ChaCha12") -- the word "currently" is the tell. The rand crate documents StdRng as explicitly NOT reproducible across versions or platforms. Determinism is this repo crown jewel; byte-exact grading, WASM parity, and every golden rest on assembly being reproducible. Resting that on an RNG whose own docs disclaim the guarantee is a latent break: a dependency bump silently changes assembled exams.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A portable PRNG is named and pinned (algorithm + version), independent of rand default-feature drift.
- The shuffle/sampling algorithm is SPECIFIED in the crate docs, not merely implemented.
- Cross-version test: the same seed produces the same item ids under a pinned-and-bumped dependency matrix.
- Native and WASM produce identical assembled sets for the same seed (extend the existing dual-path parity beyond grading into assembly and choice shuffling).
- Known-bad injection: swap the PRNG -> golden assembly RED. Meta-test: delete the parity assertion -> selftest non-zero.

title: C5: module 15 is assessed but never taught — decide and record
description:
WHAT: resolve the 15-ops-adjacent module: give it a Learn surface, or exclude it from assembly. Record which and why.

WHY: knowledge/domains.toml declares 15-ops-adjacent; the bank holds 39 items for it; web/content/modules/ has 14 modules and no module 15; cdcp_assemble samples across every bank module. A learner can therefore be scored on material the course does not contain. This is a live FAIRNESS defect, disclosed in CHARTER 2026-08-14 but not yet resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A recorded decision (bead comment + CHARTER edit): teach or exclude.
- If EXCLUDE: assembly rejects module 15; a known-bad injection proves an ops-adjacent item cannot enter an assembled exam; the 39 items are marked retired or moved out of the assessed pool.
- If TEACH: a Learn surface exists for module 15 and the doc-truth gate confirms module count agreement across CHARTER/README/FEATURE_SURFACE.
- Either way: a gate asserts that EVERY module present in the assembled pool has a corresponding Learn surface. Anti-vacuous: zero modules compared is an ERROR.
- L9 supplied a 28-Gap curriculum for this module, each with a named free-to-redistribute primary source -- consult it before choosing EXCLUDE.
close_reason: C5 shipped 6517ea5. DECISION: teach, not exclude — recorded in CHARTER §11 row 8 with the reasoning (the buyer is a facilities-hybrid seat and ops discipline is the most interview-probed body of knowledge for it; excluding would have bought fairness by deleting what the buyer is hired for). Controller-verified independently: web/content/modules/15-ops-adjacent.md is 47,901 bytes / 7,211 words, and web/learn/15-ops-adjacent.html carries data-content-href=../content/modules/15-ops-adjacent.md with a tag skeleton IDENTICAL to module 14's, so it loads by the same offline path as the other 14. My first measurement counted the shell (131 words) and was wrong, not the agent's claim. Learner-visible change: a missed ops-adjacent item now yields a working 'Review in Learn' link, which it did not before — MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS in results.js was hardcoded 1-14. Guard: crates/cdcp_assemble/tests/learn_surface_coverage.rs, proven to trip on the real tree (primary_notes reverted -> RED 'modules are ASSESSED but never TAUGHT: [15]'). Residual filed as bd-lt7: three gates had encoded the defect as a rule.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION: TEACH (not exclude). Recorded in CHARTER §11 row 8 + §3 Learn row (edited in place).

WHY TEACH, when C1 made exclude a one-field change:
Both options close the fairness defect; only one improves the product. The buyer (CHARTER §1)
is targeting a facilities-hybrid seat, and operations discipline is the most interview-probed
body of knowledge for that seat. Excluding would have made the exam fair by deleting the
material the buyer is hired for — fairness bought by making the course smaller in its most
valuable area. C1 deliberately left the decision open precisely so it would be argued on
product value rather than on implementation cost, and cheapness is not an argument.

The cost was bounded, not open-ended: research lineage L9 had already read 20 primary documents
and emitted a 28-unit curriculum, each with a named free-to-redistribute source. The full L9
synthesis (67KB) was on disk. This was curation, not original research.

WHAT A LEARNER EXPERIENCES DIFFERENTLY
- The Learn hub lists 15 modules, not 14. web/learn/15-ops-adjacent.html is a full, navigable
  reader page (7,183 words) with TOC, 7 lesson units and micro-checks (units 127 -> 134).
- All six topics the 39 items assess now deep-link into the module:
    m15-labelling / m15-documentation / m15-cleaning / m15-mtbf-mttr /
    m15-maintenance-sla / m15-ops-security  -> learn/15-ops-adjacent.html#<anchor>
- Missing an ops-adjacent item now yields a working "Review section in Learn" link. It did not
  before: MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS in web/assets/js/results.js was hardcoded 1-14, so an m15 miss
  produced a dead end. That was a second, unlogged instance of the same defect.
- The module is labelled in-page and in domains.toml as exam_weight_unknown and NOT one of the
  14 public EPI domains, so the honesty constitution is unchanged.

CONTENT GROUNDING (all freely redistributable, per honesty constitution §4)
29 CFR 1910.147/.333/.269, 10 CFR 26.205, DOE O 422.1, DOE-STD-1029-92, DOE-HDBK-1028-2009,
DOE/PNNL O&M Best Practices Guide R3.0, NASA RCM Guide, NIST SP 800-61r2, FEMA NIMS 2017,
HSE HSG250 + CHIS6, U.S.-Canada Outage Task Force 2004, CAIB Vol I Ch.8, Cloudflare PDX-04.
Licensed/paywalled sources (NFPA 70E/70B, ASHRAE 135/BACnet, ISA-18.2, EEMUA 191, ISO 14644,
Uptime Tier/M&O) are NAMED AND NOT QUOTED, with the BACnet hole stated in-page as a gap rather
than filled from a secondary summary. Google SRE is cited, not reproduced (CC BY-NC-ND).
L9 unit 28 (evidence hygiene) is included: the domain's most-quoted human-error statistic has
no obtainable primary source, and the module teaches that as the worked example.

THE TEST
crates/cdcp_assemble/tests/learn_surface_coverage.rs — 10 #[test], no .py/.sh.
  every_assessed_module_has_a_learn_surface: modules holding >=1 approved bank item MUST be a
  subset of modules with a navigable Learn surface (index row not empty, relative href, and
  web/learn/{id}.html + web/content/modules/{id}.md both present on disk).
ANTI-VACUOUS: three emptiness guards each panic rather than skip —
  anti_vacuous_empty_assessed_set_is_an_error, anti_vacuous_empty_index_is_an_error
  (incl. an index of nothing but empty-ok rows), plus loaders that assert rather than return.
GATE PROVEN TO TRIP, on the real tree, not just on fixtures: reverting domains.toml
primary_notes to "" and rebuilding turned it RED with
  "modules are ASSESSED but never TAUGHT: [15]" and
  "module 15 holds approved bank items but its Learn row is empty-ok" (8 passed / 2 failed).
Restored to green. known_bad_empty_ok_row_does_not_count_as_taught reproduces the exact
pre-C5 shipped state, which an id-presence check would have called green for the whole life
of the defect.
The EXCLUDE branch stays lawful: excluding_a_module_from_the_pool_also_satisfies_the_gate
passes, so a future tick can retire a module's items without editing the test.

TWO STALE EXEMPTIONS REMOVED (both restated the defect as a rule)
- scripts/smoke_learn.py asserted "hub must not link to empty-ok ops-adjacent module page",
  hardcoded to module 15. Rewritten to derive empty ids from the index — a gate naming one id
  cannot notice the next one.
- scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py skipped module>14 items as "ops-adjacent: no Learn page
  required". That exemption is gone; an item on a form whose module has no Learn surface is now
  an ERROR. Proven to trip (removing 14 from the slug map -> 3 named failures), restored.
  Now reports untaught_module_items=0 (must be 0), 40/40 module links resolve.

VERIFICATION
verify_doc_consistency.py EXIT 0 (roadmap GREEN, 3 docs, 29 milestone rows, 0 conflicts).
cargo fmt --check 0 · clippy -D warnings 0 · cargo test --locked --workspace all green.
registry-check OK · goldens check ok (all three) · content.lock regenerated + verified.
verify_bank / validate_grounding / verify_orphans / verify_coverage / verify_objectives /
verify_knowledge_paths / smoke_learn / smoke_learn_v2 / smoke_learn_chrome / smoke_a11y /
smoke_weak_links / smoke_feedback_links / smoke_slo / export_anki — all PASS.
bank_hash UNCHANGED (e82817572a82…): no bank item was touched.

WIRING NEEDED (scripts/check.sh not edited, per constraint)
None. The new suite is a tests/ target in cdcp_assemble, so `cargo test --locked --workspace`
(check.sh line 176) already runs it. No new check.sh step required.

SEPARATE DEFECTS FOUND (not fixed here)
1. results.js MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS was hardcoded 1-14 — fixed here as part of the decision, but
   the class of bug (a JS map that must stay in sync with domains.toml and has no gate binding
   them) is unaddressed. smoke_feedback_links now covers it for modules on the seed42 form only.
2. verify_coverage.py PRIMARY_MODULES is range(1,15) and build_units.py's micro-check floor is
   `int(m[:2]) <= 14`. Module 15 is therefore taught and assessed but exempt from the coverage
   floor and the >=80%-units-with->=2-checks floor. It happens to satisfy both today (39 items,
   7/7 units with >=2 checks) — by luck, not by gate. Worth a follow-up bead.
3. Goldens were transiently dirty mid-run from another agent's known-bad injection
   (goldens/*.sha256 held the all-f sentinel at 23:08). Self-corrected; `goldens check` green
   at close. Not caused by this work — flagging only because a crashed selftest would leave the
   tree in that state silently.
4. README.md badge "36 injections" counts shell-selftest receipts only. The 6 new Rust known-bad
   legs are not in that ledger by design; if the badge is meant to mean "all known-bad
   injections", it now understates.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
ADDENDUM — a third stale 1-14 bound, and one blocker owned by another agent.

5. scripts/smoke_weak_links.py had the same defect-shaped exemption as the other two, but
   inverted: it hard-coded `range(1, 15)` and REJECTED module 15 as
   "unexpected MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS keys: [15]". A correct fix to the product was failing a
   gate for being correct. Rebased on EXPECTED_SLUGS instead of a literal range, and its
   modules_index cross-check now ERRORS on a navigable module with no slug entry rather than
   `continue`-ing past it. Proven to trip both ways: removing 15 from results.js ->
   "module 15: missing from MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS"; restored -> PASS with M15 listed.

   Three gates (smoke_learn, smoke_feedback_links, smoke_weak_links) each independently
   encoded "module 15 is the untaught one" as a rule. That is the real finding: the defect
   had been normalised into the gate layer, so the gates would have resisted any fix. Worth
   a follow-up bead to sweep for other hard-coded module bounds — verify_coverage.py
   (PRIMARY_MODULES = range(1,15)) and build_units.py (`int(m[:2]) <= 14`) still carry them,
   as noted in item 2 of the previous comment.

BLOCKER, NOT MINE, NOT FIXED (constraint: do not touch web/diagrams/ or another agent's files)
   `cargo test --locked --workspace` has exactly one failure:
     cdcp_registry_check tests::real_repo_is_clean
     load_bearing_uncited — docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md: load-bearing phrase class 'grade-exact'
     matched but file lacks markers for ["claim-grade-byte-exact"]
   `cargo run -p cdcp_registry_check` returned OK (L1 green) earlier in this same session;
   docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md was then modified at 23:11 alongside four new untracked
   web/diagrams/*.html files. This is the diagrams agent mid-flight, unrelated to module 15,
   and it is theirs to resolve — the file needs a [[claim:claim-grade-byte-exact]] marker or
   the phrase softened. Flagging so it is not mistaken for C5 fallout.

STATUS: acceptance met, bead left OPEN and UNCOMMITTED per dispatch constraint (no git commit).
Every other gate green; see previous comment for the full list.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
ADDENDUM 2 — a data-loss bug in build_learn.py, found by running it.

6. scripts/build_learn.py's orphan sweep (`for stale in CONTENT_DIR.glob("*.md")`) deletes any
   .md in web/content/modules/ that is not a navigable module id. web/content/modules/README.md
   is hand-written, tracked documentation and matched that filter, so EVERY run of build_learn.py
   silently deletes it. Confirmed by `git status` after my first build: `D web/content/modules/README.md`.
   This is pre-existing and not specific to module 15 — anyone who has run build_learn.py since
   the README was added has been deleting it, and it would ride along in the next commit.

title: C6: min_modules is accepted and ignored
description:
WHAT: enforce the min_modules constraint or delete the parameter.

WHY: cdcp_assemble takes `_min_modules: usize` (underscore-prefixed = deliberately unused) at one call site while cfg.min_modules is passed elsewhere and asserted in a test. A configuration knob that is accepted, documented, and silently ignored is worse than an absent one: callers believe a constraint is enforced.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Either min_modules is enforced on every assembly path, or the parameter is removed from the signature and config.
- If enforced: an assembly that cannot satisfy min_modules is an ERROR naming the shortfall, never a silent under-covered exam.
- Known-bad injection: request min_modules greater than the available approved module count -> ERROR, not a quiet partial result. Meta-test: delete the check -> selftest RED.
- Interacts with C1: the approved-only pool may make min_modules unsatisfiable where the full pool satisfied it. That interaction must be tested explicitly.

title: D1: Evidence<T> core — certificates that travel inside values
description:
WHAT: cdcp_evidence with NumericalCertificate {kind, lo, hi}, StatisticalCertificate, ModelEvidence {cards, assumptions, validity, discrepancy_rel, in_domain}, SensitivitySummary {d_qoi}.

WHY: adapted from frankensim fs-evidence, whose own header states the failure mode we would otherwise ship: "without model-form evidence, FrankenSim can produce beautifully certified WRONG answers." Review round 3 rejected v3 because assumptions became invisible axioms. Attaching the certificate to the value makes them visible and non-bypassable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Composition is CONSERVATIVE by construction: numerical enclosures round OUTWARD, validity domains INTERSECT, discrepancy_rel ADDS.
- Property test: for any two Evidence values, combine() never produces a tighter enclosure or wider validity domain than either input.
- discrepancy_rel rejects NaN and negatives; +inf is a valid explicit unbounded claim.
- #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no floating-point equality in composition logic.
- Known-bad injection: make composition round INWARD -> property test RED. Meta-test: delete the conservativeness assertion -> selftest non-zero.

title: D2: ValidityDomain + in_domain propagation — mechanized abstention
description:
WHAT: ValidityDomain{bounds: BTreeMap<String,(f64,f64)>} with query-time domain checking; in_domain goes FALSE the moment any constituent is queried out of domain, and propagates through composition.

WHY: this is the mechanized abstention review round 3 demanded as a PX kill condition -- "an explicit scope/abstention result when a question exceeds the semantics", with "either out-of-scope case receives a confident computed answer rather than abstention" as a FAIL. frankensim fs-convection implements it as a type: every correlation card "refuses missing or out-of-domain groups". It REPLACES the crude refuse-cooling-wholesale fidelity line from ROADMAP-WAVES.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A query outside a declared bound returns an abstention result, NOT a value with a caveat.
- in_domain=false propagates through every composition path; a test asserts it cannot be reset to true downstream.
- Reversed finite endpoints normalize; a NaN endpoint is preserved as an UNUSABLE domain (not silently dropped).
- Model cards name their idealizing assumptions explicitly.
- Known-bad injection: query a correlation 1 ulp outside its bound -> abstain. Meta-test: delete the domain check -> selftest RED.

title: D3: SourceArtifact / ClaimRecord / ReviewRecord / ItemEvidence
description:
WHAT: the record types behind evidence conformance. SourceArtifact{authority, edition, date, jurisdiction, licence, digest, locator}; ClaimRecord (normalized proposition with scope and qualifiers); ReviewRecord (independent human review of claim-to-source entailment); ItemEvidence (the correct option AND every plausible distractor link to accepted claims).

WHY: round 2 was explicit that a citation gate proves referential integrity, NOT that the source supports the keyed answer. Call it EVIDENCE CONFORMANCE, never a factual oracle. Also round 2: one crate, not separate cite/incident ceremony.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Changing the stem, keyed answer, proposition, or source INVALIDATES an existing approval.
- "The stem has a citation" is insufficient: distractors must link to accepted claims too.
- Paid-standard claims are supported via licensed-reviewer ATTESTATION + clause locator; public CI never re-evaluates text it cannot lawfully access.
- ai_ingestion=PROHIBITED sources (ASHRAE) can carry a locator + human attestation but MUST NOT carry extracted text.
- Known-bad injection: mutate a keyed answer without re-review -> approval invalid, RED.

title: D4: licence policy enforcement — the three-field split
description:
WHAT: enforce the rights/redistribution/ai_ingestion split shipped in P0 as a build gate, not a convention.

WHY: `access = "free"` was ONE field answering THREE unrelated questions -- price, redistribution, AI ingestion. That conflation is how three ASHRAE captures ended up in a public repo carrying oq09="VERIFIED store free PDFs in-repo". L2 stated it exactly: "access=free is about price; ASHRAE AI policy is about ingestion."

## Acceptance Criteria
- Any artifact under a PUBLISHED path whose .meta.toml records redistribution != permitted is RED, naming the file (this closes bd-ashrae-redistribution-contradiction-p5n as a class, not an instance).
- A .meta.toml with a MISSING licence/rights field is an ERROR, never default-permissive.
- An artifact declaring third_party_figures may NOT be marked redistribution=public-domain (closes bd-doe-guide-embeds-ashrae-p54 as a class).
- ai_ingestion=PROHIBITED artifacts are excluded from any agent-reachable corpus index.
- Anti-vacuous: zero artifacts scanned is an ERROR. Known-bad injections for each of the four rules + meta-tests.

title: E1: cdcp_data — licence-gated, content-addressed snapshot loader
description:
WHAT: loader for vendored public-domain snapshots. Content-addressed, no network I/O, snapshots pinned at build time.

WHY: preserves the offline-first invariant (the repo currently has ZERO network deps, by design) while making external data usable. The loader is the enforcement point for D4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- REFUSES to load an artifact whose .meta.toml lacks a licence line. Not a warning -- a refusal.
- Verifies the recorded sha256 on load; mismatch is an ERROR naming both hashes.
- No reqwest/http dependency enters the workspace (assert in CI over Cargo.lock).
- Anti-vacuous: zero artifacts loaded where >=1 is registered is an ERROR.
- Known-bad injection: strip a licence line -> load refused; corrupt one byte -> hash mismatch RED. Meta-tests for both.

title: E3: vendor OSHA/eCFR as quotable primary safety text
description:
WHAT: vendor the relevant 29 CFR parts from eCFR with .meta.toml (PD-GOV, redistribution permitted, ai_ingestion permitted).

WHY: this is the ONLY normative safety material the project may quote in full. Review round 3 forbade the plant model from ever claiming a sequence is "safe"; OSHA is the actual authority, and it is public domain. CRITICAL CORRECTION from L9 that must be encoded, because the industry and an earlier version of this plan both got it wrong: 29 CFR 1910.147(a)(1)(ii)(D) EXCLUDES exposure to electrical hazards in electric-utilization installations -- a data centre switchgear/UPS/PDU. That work falls under Subpart S, not .147. A campus with its own substation runs THREE OSHA regimes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 1910.147, 1910.269, and Subpart S vendored with verified licence lines and source URLs.
- The .147 scope exclusion is captured as a first-class fact, not a footnote; any curriculum unit citing .147 for electrical LOTO is RED.
- Concurrent maintainability is recorded as a LEGAL isolation constraint: deenergise-first; control-circuit devices and interlocks may not be the sole means of deenergizing; backfeed testing mandatory.
- Known-bad injection: an item citing 1910.147 as the electrical-LOTO authority -> RED.

title: F3: the differential harness — first real external oracle
description:
WHAT: compute quantities (free-cooling hours, seismic design values, grid carbon intensity) for known locations from vendored PD-GOV data and compare against PUBLISHED reference values from sources we do not control. Disagreement beyond a declared tolerance is RED.

WHY: THE payoff of the whole programme. Three review rounds established that citation integrity is not validation (v1) and deduction from an authored model is not truth (v3) -- both failed because WE authored the premises. NOAA did not ask us what the weather was. This is the first check in the project history that can be wrong in a way we do not control.

## Acceptance Criteria
- >=5 reference locations with published values from independent sources; each reference cited with retrieval date.
- Tolerance is DECLARED per quantity with a stated justification, never tuned after seeing results (record the tolerance in the commit that adds the reference).
- Disagreement is RED and names the location, computed value, reference value, and delta.
- Anti-vacuous: zero reference locations compared is an ERROR.
- Known-bad injection: perturb the computation by 1 tolerance unit -> RED. Meta-test: delete the comparison -> selftest non-zero.
- CHARTER L3 row flips from NO to YES ONLY when this lands, and the capability-maturity row (B1) points at this test.

title: G1: cdcp_assess — assessment kinds beyond four letters
description:
WHAT: typed assessment kinds — single-select, multi-select, ordering, numeric-range, topology-selection, procedural-sequence — with deterministic pure scoring.

WHY: ChoiceLetter is four letters (crates/cdcp_core), BankItem stores one correct letter, cdcp_assemble hard-codes four choices. Round 3: "if computed scenarios are merely flattened back into A-D, you have built a better answer-key generator inside the same recognition interface." G is the prerequisite for K and for any PX output being usable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Integer or rational arithmetic ONLY; no floating-point comparison in scoring.
- Identical fixtures produce byte-identical results native and wasm32 (extends the existing dual-path contract beyond fixed-bank grading).
- Ordering and procedural-sequence scoring define partial credit explicitly, or explicitly refuse it -- no implicit behaviour.
- numeric-range carries units and a declared tolerance; a bare number is a schema ERROR.
- Existing 804 items migrate to an explicit kind WITHOUT changing any grade (golden diff must be empty).
- Known-bad injection per kind + meta-tests.

title: Substrate Law violation: 17 Python gates on the load-bearing path in a Rust/WASM project
description:
WHAT: 17 Python scripts are wired into scripts/check.sh as load-bearing gates, in a project whose
Substrate Law requires Rust on the hot path. Measured 2026-08-14: Rust 3,763 lines · Python 6,624 ·
Shell 2,155. The "Rust/WASM" course engine is ~70% Python and shell by volume.

Gate-path Python (all invoked by check.sh):
build_glossary_json · build_units · export_anki · smoke_diagrams · smoke_feedback_links ·
smoke_learn_chrome · smoke_learn · smoke_weak_links · validate_grounding · verify_bank ·
verify_content_lock · verify_coverage · verify_doc_consistency · verify_injection_count ·
verify_knowledge_paths · verify_objectives · verify_orphans

WHY: three independent costs.

(1) DOCTRINE. The Substrate Law states that reaching for .py on a load-bearing path is a DEFECT,
and that the ONLY sanctioned Python is a throwaway test file WITH a stated Rust migration path.
None of the 17 carries one. They are permanent infrastructure wearing a temporary licence.

(2) WASM. Python gates cannot run in WebAssembly. This project's entire thesis is a pure grader
compiled to native AND wasm32 with byte-identical output. The verification layer is stranded on
the native side — a browser cannot check what it just graded. Rust gates could ship to both.

(3) THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN-REPO AND WAS IGNORED. crates/cdcp_registry_check is a Rust crate
performing L1 claims validation — precisely frankensim's tools/registry-check pattern (a dedicated
crate WITH ITS OWN TEST SUITE) and its `xtask check-goldens`. The correct architecture is
demonstrated three directories away. Three of the 17 (verify_doc_consistency, verify_orphans,
verify_injection_count) were added on 2026-08-13 BY THIS SESSION, after citing that very pattern in
docs/FRANKENSIM-ADOPTION.md. Having the right pattern in hand and writing Python anyway is the
defect worth recording.

NOT A BLANKET BAN. A THIN orchestrator in shell is correct and endorsed (beads-north-star: "keep
the orchestrator (gate.sh / xtask) THIN — assertions live in the tests, not the shell"). check.sh
calling `cargo test` and `cargo run -p <gate>` is right. What is wrong is ASSERTION LOGIC living in
.py/.sh on a gate path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A Rust gate crate (or xtask) owns the assertion logic for every check currently implemented in a
  gate-path .py file. Prefer ONE crate with subcommands over 17 binaries.
- The crate has its OWN test suite — the checker is itself checked (frankensim registry-check rule).
- check.sh becomes a thin ordered chain of `cargo run -p <gate> <subcmd>` / `cargo test` calls; no
  assertion logic remains in shell or Python on any gate path.
- Every migrated gate keeps its known-bad injection and meta-test, now as Rust #[test] — deleting
  the assertion must turn `cargo test` RED.
- Anti-vacuous preserved end to end: an empty scan set remains an ERROR, never a pass.
- The injection count (currently 36 across 9 suites, drift-guarded) must be RE-DERIVED after
  migration and the README figure updated through the drift guard, not by hand.
- Any .py that legitimately survives (e.g. a one-shot content build like build_units.py) carries an
  explicit `# RUST MIGRATION: <bead|N/A because ...>` header, and a gate asserts that header exists
  on every remaining .py under scripts/. Blank is an ERROR, not permission.
- Byte-exactness is preserved: goldens unchanged across the migration, or every change re-frozen
  with a written justification via goldens-couplings (B2).

SEQUENCING: this is large. Do NOT attempt it as one tick. Split per gate, migrate the three added
2026-08-13 FIRST (they are newest, smallest, and the ones this session owes), and land each behind
its own known-bad + meta-test. Coordinate with B2 — a gate that moves language is a semantic
surface change and its goldens must re-freeze deliberately.

title: EPIC: convert all 17 Python gates to Rust, byte-exact
description:
WHAT: convert all 17 gate-path Python scripts to Rust, byte-exact, behind ONE `cdcp_gate` crate
with subcommands. Delete the Python. check.sh becomes a thin ordered chain of cargo invocations.

WHY: measured 2026-08-14 — Rust 3,763 lines vs Python 6,624 and Shell 2,155. A Rust/WASM project
that is ~70% Python and shell, with 17 Python scripts wired into check.sh as load-bearing gates.
Three costs: (1) the Substrate Law names .py on a load-bearing path a DEFECT with no migration path
recorded on any of the 17; (2) Python gates cannot run in WASM, so a browser can grade an exam and
cannot verify what it graded — the verification layer is stranded on the native side of a project
whose thesis is byte-identical native/wasm output; (3) the correct pattern already exists in-repo
(crates/cdcp_registry_check, mirroring frankensim tools/registry-check) and was walked past.

FEASIBILITY, MEASURED: all 17 are Python-stdlib only. No numpy, lxml, pandas, or selenium. The one
apparent hard case, smoke_learn_chrome, does NOT drive a browser — "chrome" is learn_chrome.js, the
UI chrome; it is a static file check. All five smoke scripts parse with regex/string, not DOM. Only
export_anki reaches beyond stdlib (sqlite3, zipfile), both with mature Rust crates. Total 4,545
lines across 17 files.

THE MIGRATION MECHANISM IS THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: for each gate, run the Python and the Rust on
identical inputs and assert byte-identical stdout, stderr, AND exit code across every fixture
including the known-bad ones. The Python is the reference oracle for its own replacement, then is
deleted. "Did I port this correctly" stops being a judgement call.

## Success Criteria
- Zero .py and zero assertion-bearing .sh remain on any check.sh gate path.
- One `cdcp_gate` crate with subcommands; the crate has its OWN test suite (the checker is checked).
- Every migrated gate keeps its known-bad injection and meta-test, now as Rust #[test]: deleting the
  assertion turns `cargo test` RED.
- Anti-vacuous preserved end to end — an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass.
- The drift-guarded injection count (36 across 9 suites) is RE-DERIVED after migration and README is
  updated THROUGH the guard, never by hand.
- Byte-exactness: goldens unchanged, or every change re-frozen with written justification via B2.

title: S0: hard gate — no new .py/.sh may be committed without a reasoned allowlist entry
description:
WHAT: a hard gate that FAILS THE BUILD AND BLOCKS THE COMMIT when a new .py or .sh appears, unless
it carries an explicit, reasoned allowlist entry. Ships BEFORE the 17-gate migration — it stops the
bleeding while the cleanup proceeds.

WHY: measured 2026-08-14, this repo is ~70% Python/shell by volume with 17 Python gates on the
check.sh path, and THREE of those were added on 2026-08-13 by a session that had just documented the
correct Rust pattern. Prohibition in doctrine did not prevent it; only a gate will. Without S0, the
migration is a bucket with the tap still running.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT DEFINES THIS BEAD: **the guard that bans shell must not itself be shell.**
Assertion logic lives in Rust (`cdcp_gate substrate-guard`). The git hook may be a THIN shim whose
entire body is invoking the Rust binary — a thin orchestrator is endorsed (beads-north-star: "keep
the orchestrator THIN — assertions live in the tests, not the shell"). A shim containing any
decision logic fails this bead.

## Design
- New crate `crates/cdcp_gate`, subcommand `substrate-guard`. This is also the scaffold every later
  migration bead extends, so get its shape right: subcommands, shared exit-code conventions, its own
  test suite.
- `registries/substrate_allowlist.toml`: one row per permitted non-Rust file —
  `{ path, reason, migration_bead, expires }`.
- Enforcement is on ADDITION and on PRESENCE: a new unlisted file is RED, and a listed file whose
  row lost its reason is RED.
- Two call sites: (1) `scripts/check.sh` as an ordered step; (2) `.git/hooks/pre-commit` shim, plus
  a committed `hooks/pre-commit` and an install step, because a hook that only exists on one machine
  is not a gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A newly added `.py` or `.sh` anywhere under `scripts/`, `crates/`, or repo root with NO allowlist
  row makes `check.sh` RED and `git commit` FAIL, naming the file and the bead to file.
- An allowlist row with a MISSING or EMPTY `reason` is a schema ERROR, not permission. Blank is
  never permissive (house rule, same as corpus licence fields).
- An allowlist row past its `expires` date is RED — a temporary exemption that cannot expire is
  permanent by another name.
- KNOWN-GOOD LEG (mandatory, this gate is easy to make over-strict): an allowlisted file with a
  valid reason passes; editing an EXISTING allowlisted file does not trip the gate; a `.rs` file
  added anywhere passes. An attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate and over-strict gates get
  routed around.
- KNOWN-BAD injections, all must go RED: add unlisted `scripts/foo.py`; add unlisted `scripts/foo.sh`;
  strip the `reason` from a row; backdate an `expires`.
- META-TEST: delete the guard's assertion -> `cargo test -p cdcp_gate` RED. Delete the check.sh step
  -> a selftest notices the step is missing (BUILT != WIRED: a gate not invoked is not installed).
- INSTALL PROOF (decalogue 10): show the hook firing on a real `git commit` attempt WITHOUT anyone
  invoking it by hand, and paste the refusal.
- Anti-vacuous: zero files scanned is an ERROR, not a pass.
- The guard's own header states its claim as a FLOOR-RAISE: it enforces "no unreasoned non-Rust file
  enters the tree"; it CANNOT decide whether a stated reason is honest. Say so in the header. No
  "guarantees/proves/makes impossible".

## Seed the allowlist honestly
The 17 existing gates go in with `migration_bead` pointing at their per-gate migration bead and a
real `expires`. They are grandfathered EXPLICITLY and visibly, never silently — the allowlist is the
migration worklist, and it should shrink to zero.
close_reason: S0 substrate floor installed, wired, and observed denying a real commit. Controller re-ran every acceptance criterion independently: unlisted .py/.sh -> exit 2 naming the file and the bead; blank reason -> 4; expired row -> 4; known-GOOD legs (allowlisted file, edit of an existing allowlisted file, .rs added anywhere) -> 0; zero files scanned -> 4; deleted check.sh step -> 2 (BUILT != WIRED); neutered assertion -> cargo test 101 with 4 named failures, restored -> 0; real git commit refused, HEAD unmoved. Graded 955/1000, Verified band, threshold 700. Residuals tracked as bd-u2x and .19/.20, not waived.

title: PORT 1: verify_orphans.py -> cdcp_gate verify_orphans (byte-exact)
description:
WHAT: port `scripts/verify_orphans.py` (176 lines) to Rust as `cdcp_gate verify_orphans`, byte-exact, then DELETE the
Python and remove its allowlist row.

WHY: Added 2026-08-13 by the session that had just documented the correct Rust pattern in FRANKENSIM-ADOPTION.md. Session debt, paid first.

## The migration mechanism IS the acceptance criterion
Run the Python and the Rust on identical inputs. Assert **byte-identical stdout, byte-identical
stderr, and identical exit code** across every fixture — the clean tree, every known-bad specimen,
and the anti-vacuous empty-input case. The Python is the reference oracle for its own replacement.
"Did I port this correctly" is then measured, not judged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cdcp_gate verify_orphans` produces byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit to `python3 scripts/verify_orphans.py` on: the live
  tree; every known-bad fixture the original had; an EMPTY input set (must remain an ERROR, never a
  pass); and any --flag combination check.sh uses.
- A differential test asserting the above lives in `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/` and runs in CI while
  BOTH implementations exist.
- Any behavioural difference found is a FINDING: record whether the Python or the Rust is correct
  before changing either. Do NOT silently adopt the Rust behaviour — a port that "fixes" a bug while
  claiming byte-exactness has broken the oracle.
- Known-bad injection preserved as a Rust #[test]; meta-test — delete the assertion, `cargo test -p
  cdcp_gate` goes RED.
- `scripts/verify_orphans.py` is DELETED and its `registries/substrate_allowlist.toml` row removed in the same
  commit. The allowlist shrinking IS the progress metric.
- check.sh invokes the Rust subcommand; no Python remains on this gate path.
- If this gate contributes known-bad injections to the drift-guarded count (currently 36/9 suites),
  the count is RE-DERIVED through the guard, never hand-edited.

## File ownership (parallel-safe)
Own ONLY: `crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_orphans.rs`, `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_orphans.rs`, and the deletion
of `scripts/verify_orphans.py`. Do NOT edit `mod.rs`, `main.rs`, `check.sh`, or the allowlist — REPORT the exact
lines needed and the orchestrator wires them. Concurrent agents are porting sibling gates.

title: Seed-42 golden pins Python MT19937 output; the Rust sampler is never exercised
description:
WHAT: goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json was generated by scripts/sample_mock.py (Python MT19937).
cdcp_cli export-web PREFERS that fixture whenever seed == 42 (main.rs:79 default_value). The Rust
assemble() at seed 42 produces a DIFFERENT 40-item set — 5+ ids differ each way. Therefore
"goldens check" never exercises the Rust sampler.

WHY: this is a FOOLED CERTIFICATE. A golden that reads as evidence the Rust assembler is
deterministic is in fact pinning the output of a Python script. Both implementations are internally
deterministic; they simply disagree, and the fixture preference hides the disagreement.

Three consequences:
1. Assembly determinism is UNTESTED end to end. The gate that appears to cover it covers something
   else.
2. C4 (portable PRNG) is more urgent than filed. StdRng is not merely non-portable in theory — the
   assembler's live output already disagrees with the pinned artifact.
3. THE SUBSTRATE MIGRATION WOULD HAVE DELETED THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. sample_mock.py is not on
   the 17-gate list, but a sweep removing Python takes the only artifact that can explain what the
   fixture contains, leaving a golden nobody can regenerate or justify. Sequence this BEFORE the
   migration reaches it.

Found by the C1 agent while verifying its own seed-42 diff; independently confirmed at
crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs:48,79 and scripts/sample_mock.py header.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A recorded decision on which implementation is CORRECT — the Python MT19937 stratification or the
  Rust sampler. Do NOT silently adopt whichever is more convenient; the divergence is a finding and
  the reasoning goes in the bead before either changes.
- The seed-42 golden is regenerated by the AUTHORITATIVE implementation, and export-web no longer
  bypasses the sampler at any seed (or the bypass is retained with an explicit, tested reason).
- A test asserts the Rust assemble() output at a pinned seed MATCHES the golden — i.e. the golden
  exercises the sampler it claims to certify. Known-bad: perturb the sampler, golden goes RED.
- Registered as a SEMANTIC SURFACE in goldens-couplings (B2) so any future re-freeze is deliberate
  and justified.
- Coordinate with C4: whatever PRNG is chosen must be portable and named, and the golden re-frozen
  under it once.
- Until resolved, scripts/sample_mock.py is PINNED — it may not be deleted by the substrate
  migration. Add it to the substrate allowlist with this bead as its migration_bead.
close_reason: Shipped 6517ea5. Measured 37 of 40 seed-42 ids differed between sample_mock.py (CPython MT19937) and cdcp_assemble, not the 5+ this bead assumed — and the fixture was reproducible by NEITHER, because the bank drifted while regen_goldens_after_bank.py froze item_ids. It was an orphaned artifact, not a reference. Rust sampler is now authoritative; the implicit seed==42 fixture preference is deleted from export_web and --fixture survives as an explicit, tested opt-in. Controller-verified: check.sh reports export-web ... golden_pinned=false, so the shipped path now runs the sampler. Two residuals filed rather than silently absorbed: bd-z3x (regen_goldens_after_bank.py now MANUFACTURES the divergence it is checked against) and the corrected sample_mock.py allowlist row (short fuse, DO-NOT-REGENERATE banner).

comments.text:
(Disregard the preceding one-word comment — a shell heredoc misfire from this agent, no content.)

## MEASURED DIVERGENCE (step 1 — before any change)

Rust seed-42 sample obtained by running `cdcp export-web --seed 42` from a cwd where the relative
fixture path does not resolve, so the seed-42 bypass could not fire (golden_pinned=false confirmed
in stdout). Bank: 804 items, bank_hash e82817572a82d13fad699393aab97613bdc0cf4c8503e264af490dc8dd7b71db.

SET-LEVEL: 37 of 40 ids differ each way. The bead said "5+"; the true figure is 37/40.
  intersection = 3 ids only: m02-q085, bank-m15-q143, m13-q210
ORDER-LEVEL: also fully divergent — 0 of the 3 shared ids sit at the same index.
  The divergence is set-level AND order-level, not a permutation of one set.

STRATIFICATION: PRESERVED EQUALLY BY BOTH. Measured per-module counts:
  both cover all 15 modules; both peak at 3 items/module; both satisfy
  max_per_module=8 and min_modules=8. There is NO stratification-quality argument
  for either implementation. The divergence is the PRNG stream, not the algorithm.
  (CPython random.Random = MT19937 vs cdcp_assemble StdRng = ChaCha12.)

SECOND, LARGER FINDING — THE GOLDEN IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE BY ITS OWN PROVENANCE COMMAND.
  goldens/PROVENANCE.md states the fixture was made by
    python3 scripts/sample_mock.py --seed 42 --out goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json
  Re-running that command TODAY yields a different 40-item set: 17 shared, 23 differ.
  Cause: the bank drifted. Committed fixture bank_fingerprint = 0557953e8a49a3cf;
  live bank fingerprint = 5ff22c310349b2bd. scripts/regen_goldens_after_bank.py explicitly
  "does NOT reshuffle mock40 item_ids (fixture stays golden-pinned)", so bank_hash.txt and the
  grade digests were re-pinned against a growing bank while item_ids stayed frozen at the
  2026-08-11 snapshot.
  => The fixture is an ORPHANED artifact. NEITHER implementation reproduces it today.
     It is not a reference for anything; it is a frozen accident.

## DECISION (step 2): the RUST sampler `cdcp_assemble::assemble()` is AUTHORITATIVE.

Reasoning, in the order it decided the question:

1. THE PYTHON SIDE HAS NO CLAIM LEFT. The committed fixture is not what sample_mock.py produces
   today (23/40 differ). Adopting "Python" would not mean adopting the fixture — it would mean
   regenerating the fixture from Python, a change of the same magnitude as adopting Rust. The
   convenience argument for keeping the fixture as-is evaporates once you measure it.
2. RUST IS THE SHIPPED PATH. cdcp_assemble is what export-web runs at every seed != 42, what the
   product's practice forms come from, and what cdcp_wasm grades against. sample_mock.py ships to
   nobody. Pinning a shipped artifact to a non-shipped script is the defect, not the fix.
3. SUBSTRATE LAW. No .py on a load-bearing path. Declaring Python authoritative would permanently
   couple the seed-42 golden to a file the substrate migration is scheduled to delete — the exact
   trap this bead was filed to prevent.
4. NO QUALITY DIFFERENCE TO TRADE AWAY. Measured above: identical module breadth (15), identical
   peak per-module count (3), both inside policy. Choosing Rust costs nothing on the axis the
   sampler exists to serve.
5. RUST ENFORCES GATES PYTHON DOES NOT. sample_item_ids() filters to status==approved (C1) and
   hard-errors on NoApprovedItems / PoolTooSmall / ApprovedTooFewModules. sample_mock.py has no
   status concept and would silently draw draft/retired items. The filter is currently a NO-OP
   (804/804 approved) — not a cause of today's divergence, but a correctness property only Rust has.

Rejected alternative: keep Python authoritative and port MT19937 to Rust. That would import a
non-CSPRNG and a Python-shaped byte-stream contract into the shipped crate in order to preserve an
artifact that is already unreproducible. No.

## C4 INTERACTION (does not pre-empt C4)

This bead does NOT choose the PRNG. It pins the CURRENT PRNG's output and makes it observable.
When C4 replaces StdRng with a portable PRNG, the new assertion (assemble(42).item_ids == golden
fixture item_ids) goes RED — which is the correct and desired behaviour: C4 must re-freeze the
golden once, deliberately, under the portable PRNG. That re-freeze is now a visible gate trip
instead of a silent no-op, because before this bead export-web never called the sampler at seed 42
at all.
