title: Class sweep: ten public corpus captures recorded redistribution=not-licensed are published
description:
WHAT: ten body captures under knowledge/corpus/public/ are committed to a PUBLIC repo while manifest.json records each of them rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed":

  src-epi-cdcp-page, src-exin-cdcp-page, src-nh-cdcp, src-tuv-22237,
  src-en-50600-overview, src-tia-942, src-tia-942-c-fotc, src-uptime-tiers,
  src-ocp-ready, src-curriculum-map-local

WHY: this is the SAME defect class already fixed for the two ASHRAE rows under bd-ashrae-redistribution-contradiction-p5n on 2026-08-14 -- retaining a capture for internal grounding and publishing it worldwide are different acts, and the second IS redistribution, which the manifest itself records as not licensed. These ten differ from the ASHRAE pair only in that no publisher AI policy aggravates them. The legal act is identical.

They were NOT removed in that pass, deliberately and on the record: scripts/validate_grounding.py consumes these bodies as its grounding corpus (~601k chars across 804 scanned items). Deleting them without a replacement grounding source would take the build red under four concurrently active agents. That is a cross-cutting change that needs its own bead, not one smuggled into an ASHRAE fix.

They are tracked, not tolerated. Each carries rights_review="OPEN" + rights_review_bead + rights_review_reason in manifest.json, and they are listed under [[open_violation]] in knowledge/corpus/rights-policy.toml. This is a reasoned, bead-referenced exception (CORPUS-R4), not a widened allowlist.

INVARIANT BEING VIOLATED -- CORPUS-R1 (knowledge/corpus/rights-policy.toml):
  no record with redistribution != "permitted" may be capture="body-retained" with a path inside the published tree.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide per source: is redistribution actually permitted (some may be -- OCP specs carry named open licences per document, and src-curriculum-map-local is our own local file that may simply be mis-recorded), or must the body go?
  * If permitted: correct rights/redistribution to the true value with evidence, and the row legitimately stays body-retained.
  * If not: replace with capture="citation-only" carrying {url, title, publisher, fetched_at, rights, redistribution} and zero publisher-derived prose, exactly as the ASHRAE rows were handled.
- Give validate_grounding.py a grounding source that does not depend on unlicensed publisher prose, BEFORE removing bodies. This is the actual blocker; without it the removal is a build break, not a fix.
- After the sweep, [[open_violation]] in rights-policy.toml is EMPTY, and the D4 corpus-rights gate can run CORPUS-R1 with no exceptions.
- Known-bad injection still trips (fixtures already declared in rights-policy.toml [[known_bad]]).

NON-GOALS: do not rewrite git history for these; the ASHRAE HEAD-only reasoning in docs/flywheel/PREPUBLISH-SCRUB-2026-08-14.md applies a fortiori (public web-page captures, no standards body text, repo already public).

DEPENDS ON / RELATED: bd-ashrae-redistribution-contradiction-p5n (done), bd-doe-guide-embeds-ashrae-p54 (done), D4 corpus-rights Rust gate (enforces CORPUS-R1..R6 against rights-policy.toml).

title: Gate layer encodes known defects as invariants — rebase off derived facts, not hardcoded bounds
description:
WHAT: Sweep the gate layer for assertions that encode a KNOWN DEFECT as an
invariant, so that fixing the defect fails the gate. Rebase each off derived
facts instead of hardcoded bounds. Add a meta-test per gate proving the gate
still trips on the real bad input after the rebase.

WHY: Found 2026-08-14 while teaching module 15 (C5). Module 15 was assessed but
never taught — the fairness defect C5 closed. THREE independent gates had, over
time, written that defect down as a rule:

  - smoke_learn.py          asserted the hub MUST NOT link to module 15
  - smoke_feedback_links.py skipped module > 14 as "no Learn page required"
  - smoke_weak_links.py     REJECTED module 15 keys as "unexpected"

So the correct fix FAILED THREE GATES FOR BEING CORRECT. An agent without the
context to recognise this would read three red gates as three reasons the fix is
wrong, revert, and leave the defect in place with more evidence behind it than
before. That is worse than an ungated defect: the gate layer has become an
immune system attacking the repair.

THE CLASS, which is the point of this bead: a gate written by observing what the
tree currently does will encode the tree's current defects as requirements. The
defect is not "someone hardcoded 14". It is that the assertion was derived from
OBSERVED STATE rather than from a stated contract. Two sibling instances found
the same day, same root cause, unrelated subsystems:

  - smoke_diagrams.py hardcoded PRESENT to the three P0 diagrams, so it reported
    green without looking at four new P1 diagrams. FIXED (derives from
    docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md), 3 -> 7.
  - The migration epic enumerated "17 Python gates" from a remembered count;
    smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py were on the check.sh path and in no
    port bead. FIXED (.19/.20 filed).

Known remaining instances (C5 finding 3), both currently satisfied BY LUCK and
not by gate:
  - scripts/verify_coverage.py  range(1,15)  exempts module 15 from the coverage floor
  - scripts/build_units.py      <= 14        exempts module 15 from the micro-check floor

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify_coverage and build_units derive their module set from the same source
  the bank and Learn index use, not from a literal bound. Module 15 is subject to
  the coverage and micro-check floors, or its exemption is a RECORDED row with a
  reason, never a range literal.
- Each rebased gate ships a known-bad injection proving it still trips, AND a
  known-GOOD leg proving it does not refuse legitimate work.
- A grep for numeric module bounds (14, 15, range(1,15), <= 14) across scripts/
  and crates/ returns either zero hits or hits that are each justified in place.
- Anti-vacuous: zero modules discovered is an ERROR in every rebased gate.
- Meta-test per gate: delete the assertion -> selftest non-zero; restore -> 0.
  True exit codes recorded, never read through a pipe.

title: regen_goldens_after_bank.py manufactures the divergence it is checked against
description:
WHAT: scripts/regen_goldens_after_bank.py must call `cdcp goldens fixture`, or be
retired. Today it re-pins every derived digest around FROZEN item_ids.

WHY: Its stated behavior — "does NOT reshuffle mock40 item_ids" — is the exact
mechanism that produced bd-golden-sampler-divergence-09q. Measured 2026-08-14:
goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json could not be reproduced by its own
provenance command. Re-running scripts/sample_mock.py --seed 42 today yields
23/40 different ids, because the bank drifted (fixture bank_fingerprint
0557953e8a49a3cf vs live 5ff22c310349b2bd) while this script froze item_ids and
re-pinned the digests around them. NEITHER implementation reproduced the
committed fixture: it was an orphaned artifact, not a reference.

Post-fix the hazard inverts and gets sharper. cdcp_cli now asserts the fixture
equals cdcp_assemble's output for seed 42. Running this script after a bank edit
re-pins the digests while leaving item_ids stale, which turns that assertion RED
— so the script now MANUFACTURES the divergence its own output is checked
against. A repair tool that reintroduces the fault is worse than no tool,
because it is reached for precisely when someone is trying to fix things.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either: the script regenerates item_ids via `cdcp goldens fixture` (which calls
  cdcp_assemble) before re-pinning any derived digest; or it is deleted and its
  substrate_allowlist row is deleted in the same commit.
- If retained: running it after a bank edit leaves `cargo test -p cdcp_cli`
  GREEN. Prove it — edit a bank item, run the script, run the test, record the
  true exit code.

title: Flip ported gates from oracle exit codes to cdcp_gate 0/2/3/4 — one commit, after the oracles die
description:
WHAT: After every port lands and the Python oracles are deleted, flip all ported
gates from the oracle's exit codes to cdcp_gate's convention in ONE commit:
0 ok / 2 violation / 3 usage / 4 error. Update crate::exit's doc, check.sh, and
every selftest that asserts a specific code.

WHY: A real fork, raised by the verify_orphans port agent 2026-08-14 rather than
resolved silently — which is why this bead exists instead of a surprise.

crate::exit states "every ported gate returns these and only these" (0/2/3/4).
scripts/verify_orphans.py exits 1 on failure and writes nothing to stderr. Those
cannot both hold. Routing a port through GateError changes the exit code AND adds
a stderr line on every RED, so the differential test — the only mechanism that
can tell a port BUG from an intended FIX — would fail on every red case for
reasons that have nothing to do with the port's correctness.

DECISION (controller, 2026-08-14): byte-exactness wins DURING the migration.
Ported gates reproduce the oracle's exit code, including `std::process::exit(1)`,
and document the departure in the module header. This is safe downstream because
check.sh invokes every gate as `cmd || fail "..."`, which distinguishes only zero
from non-zero; no caller reads the specific code today. Verified before deciding.

The convention is not being abandoned, it is being SEQUENCED. Once an oracle is
deleted there is nothing left to be byte-exact against, and the code becomes free.
Doing it per-gate as each port lands would leave the crate in a mixed state where
a reader cannot tell which convention a given gate follows — worse than either
convention consistently applied.

RISK IF THIS BEAD IS LOST: the crate ships with cdcp_gate's own guard on 0/2/4
and its ported gates on 0/1, with a doc comment asserting a uniformity that does
not hold. That is a false statement in the substrate, and the kind a reader stops
checking. This bead is the reason the departure is temporary rather than a lie.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Blocked until every bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.N port is closed AND its
  oracle .py is deleted with its allowlist row.
- One commit flips all gates; no mixed state is ever committed.
- crate::exit's doc comment matches reality at every commit in between — if the
  mixed state persists, the doc says so explicitly with a pointer to this bead.
- Every selftest asserting a numeric exit code is updated in the same commit.
- Anti-vacuous: a gate returning 0 on an input it could not evaluate is an ERROR
  (4), never a pass, under the new convention.
- Meta-test: a gate forced to violate returns exactly 2; forced to error, 4.

title: verify_orphans.py fails open on 'items = []' — a never-checked bank file reports as passed
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_orphans.py `load_items()` fails open on `items = []`. A bank
file whose entire body is `items = []` is scanned, contributes zero items, and
produces NO error and NO mention. Fix so a file yielding zero items is an ERROR.

WHY: Found 2026-08-14 by the verify_orphans port agent, reproduced faithfully in
the Rust port rather than fixed, and pinned in
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_orphans.rs under a KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT comment
so a change to either side breaks loudly.

    if "items" in data and isinstance(data["items"], list):
        for it in data["items"]: ...      # empty list -> adds nothing, no error
    elif "id" in data: ...
    else: errors.append(f"{path.name}: no id or items[]")

The `elif` never runs for an empty list, so the else-branch that would have
caught it never runs either. Verified empirically: dropping `items = []` into the
specimen bank leaves BOTH implementations at PASS, items=804, rc=0, byte-identical.

This is decalogue rule 3 — "an empty input set is an ERROR, never a pass" —
violated at FILE granularity while the script's own docstring asserts it at
WHOLE-BANK granularity. That gap is the whole defect: a file that was never
really checked reports exactly like one that passed, and the aggregate count
still looks healthy because 804 other items carried it.

Fixed in the Python FIRST, not the Rust, so the differential test keeps working:
change the oracle, watch diff_verify_orphans.rs go RED, then change the port to
match. Fixing the Rust first would make the port non-byte-exact and the test
would flag the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A bank file yielding zero items is reported by name and is non-zero exit.
- Known-bad: `items = []` planted in the live bank -> RED, names the file.
- Known-GOOD: a legitimate single-item file (`id = ...` form, no `items` key)
  still passes — the elif branch must not be broken by the fix.
- diff_verify_orphans.rs updated in the SAME commit; its KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT
  comment is deleted, not amended, because the defect is gone.
- Meta-test: delete the new assertion -> non-zero; restore -> 0. True exit codes.

title: Drift guard has three holes — word-spelled counts invisible, wrong file reported, --require double-counts
description:
WHAT: Close three holes in verify_injection_count.py — the DRIFT GUARD itself.
Found 2026-08-14 by its port agent, reproduced faithfully rather than fixed.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this gate is what stops the L4
"gates proven to trip" claim from decaying. It sums the known-bad injections
actually executed and compares them against the number the README advertises.
A hole in the drift guard is a hole in the mechanism that detects every other
hole — the top of the certificate chain.

HOLE 1 — a count spelled in WORDS is invisible.
`_SUITE_COUNT` understands "one".."twelve"; the injection-count regex requires
`\d+`. Rewrite the README badge as "thirty-six known-bad injections" and that
check silently stops covering it. Note the shape carefully: if EVERY digit form
disappears you get "advertises no count at all" -> ERROR, so it fails closed at
the extreme. THE DANGEROUS CASE IS THE MIDDLE — a README where one of the four
advertisement sites is prose. That site just stops being checked, and the gate
stays green because the other three still parse. A partial loss of coverage that
reports identically to full coverage is the exact fooled-certificate shape.

HOLE 2 — findings hardcode `README.md:<lineno>` regardless of `--readme`.
Inside selftest_injection_count.sh this prints `README.md:3` while the file
actually under test is README_off.md. A gate that misreports WHERE the defect is
sends the next reader to an innocent file.

HOLE 3 — a suite named twice in `--require` double-counts.
`total = sum(counts.get(s, 0) for s in required)` iterates `required`, which is
`args.require.split(",")` with no dedup. `--require alpha,alpha` where alpha
reports 3 yields measured_total=6 and registered_suites=2, and prints the suite
row twice. NOT reachable from check.sh (its default roster has no duplicates) but
reachable by any other caller — and inflating measured_total is the direction
that turns a real drift GREEN. A repeated identical receipt LINE does not
double-count (dict assignment overwrites); that asymmetry is pinned by a test.

RELATED, do not fix here but read together: the README "36 injections" badge
counts shell-selftest receipts only. The Rust known-bad legs added 2026-08-14
(6 in cdcp_gate, more per port) are not in that ledger by design. So the
advertised number is drifting from the real injection count for a reason the
gate cannot see. Deciding what the badge is supposed to count is a prerequisite
to fixing hole 1 — otherwise you harden the parser around a number that is
already wrong.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_injection_count.rs go RED, then change the
port to match. Fixing the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the
differential test flags the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide and RECORD what the injections badge counts (shell receipts only, or
  shell + Rust known-bad legs). The number is regenerated, never hand-maintained.
- Word-spelled counts either parse, or a non-digit count at any advertisement
  site is itself an ERROR. Silent non-coverage is not an option.
- Findings report the file actually scanned, not a hardcoded README.md.
- `--require` dedups, or a duplicate entry is a usage ERROR.
- Known-bad per hole: badge in words -> RED; `--readme X` reporting a path other
  than X -> RED; `--require a,a` -> RED or usage error.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all three fixes.
- Meta-test, stated correctly: MUTATE the gate, confirm the diff test trips, then
  delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm it passes.
  Deleting an assertion on an unmutated tree proves nothing.

comments.author: bd-wf2 agent
comments.text:
DECISION (prerequisite) — what the injections badge counts.

The badge counts SHELL-SELFTEST RECEIPTS ONLY: the sum of `INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>`
lines emitted by the registered scripts/selftest_*.sh suites during a real check.sh run.
The Rust known-bad legs (cdcp_gate #[cfg(test)] cases, and the per-port ones landing this
wave) are NOT in the total.

Reasoning:
1. They emit no receipt. cargo test reports pass/fail, not a count, so there is nothing for
   check.sh to tee into INJ_LOG and nothing for this gate to sum. Including them means
   hand-typing a number somewhere — which is the exact defect this gate exists to remove.
2. Their count is internal to a test binary's own accounting, which the gate cannot observe.
   A Rust leg that silently stopped asserting would be invisible here WHILE inflating the
   advertised number: a fooled certificate on the certificate-checker.
3. Consequence stated honestly rather than hidden: the advertised number is a FLOOR on the
   repo's known-bad population, not its total. README now names the population on the two
   sites that explain it ("shell suites only; the Rust ports' own known-bad cases emit no
   INJECTIONS= receipt, so they are not in this total").
4. Folding them in later is a MECHANISM change, not a number change: the Rust legs must first
   emit receipts that check.sh aggregates and be registered in REGISTERED_SUITES. Until then,
   counting them would be a claim with no receipt behind it.

Recorded in scripts/verify_injection_count.py (module docstring, "WHAT THE ADVERTISED NUMBER
COUNTS"), crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_injection_count.rs (module header), and the two
README advertisement lines.

The number is now REGENERATED, not hand-typed: `--write-readme` rewrites every advertisement
site from the receipts actually collected, and refuses to write when the receipts are unsound
(missing/zero/unregistered suite, empty or missing log), so a bogus log cannot launder a wrong
number into README. Verified idempotent on the live tree: "5 site(s) already advertise 36",
README md5 unchanged.

comments.author: bd-wf2 agent
comments.text:
FIXES + EVIDENCE (ordering honoured: Python first, differential RED, then Rust).

HOLE 1 — word-spelled counts invisible. FIXED by parsing, not by erroring.
  The count token in both scanners is now `(\d+|\b(?:<english cardinal zero..ninety-nine>))`,
  hyphen and space compounds included, alternation ordered longest-first then lexicographic so
  the Rust port can rebuild the identical leftmost-first order. The `\b` guards the WORD branch
  only, so "v1.7 injections" still reads 7 while "eight" inside "freighter" does not.
  Erroring on any non-digit count was REJECTED after measurement: the live README contains
  "the known-bad injection alongside the feature" and "injections it *observed* go RED", so an
  error-on-prose rule fires on innocent lines and the gate would be edited to shut it up.
  SECOND DEFENCE for the dangerous middle case the bead names: MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES = 5 is a
  floor on how many sites must parse. The live README advertises at exactly 5 sites, and the
  selftest's specimen README writes exactly 5. A site that becomes unreadable in ANY other way
  ("three dozen", above the word vocabulary, deleted) drops the count and trips it. It is a
  floor, not an equality: adding an advertisement is free, losing one is a deliberate edit.

HOLE 2 — findings hardcoded README.md. FIXED: both findings (`advertises N known-bad
  injections` and `advertises N selftest suites`) now interpolate the path actually scanned.
  Confirmed inside the selftest's own shape: --readme README_off.md now prints
  "README_off.md:3 advertises 8 ...", and no finding names README.md.

HOLE 3 — duplicate --require. FIXED as a usage ERROR, not a silent dedup.
  Chose ERROR over dedup: a caller that names a suite twice does not know its own roster, and
  silently repairing that hides it. The gate prints FAIL + one line and exits 1 BEFORE any
  total is computed, so no measured_total is reported at all.
  The repeated-identical-receipt-LINE asymmetry is untouched and still pinned
  (a_repeated_identical_receipt_is_identical_and_not_double_counted). It is not theoretical:
  a real run shows selftest_l5.sh re-emitting selftest_l5_honesty's receipt, and the dict
  overwrite is what keeps that from inflating the total.

BEFORE (true exit codes, `cmd > log 2>&1; echo $?`):
  hole 1 middle case (3 sites digits, prose site says thirty-six)  -> exit 0  PASS (fooled)
  hole 1 sharp (one suite reporting 3 vs README saying 6)          -> exit 0  PASS (fooled)
  hole 2 (--readme README_off.md)                                  -> exit 1, 5 findings all
                                                                      naming "README.md:N"
  hole 3 (--require spec_alpha,spec_alpha)                         -> exit 1, measured_total=6
                                                                      from one suite reporting 3
  hole 3 dangerous direction (solo suite, --require a,a, README=6) -> exit 0  PASS (fooled)

DIFFERENTIAL WENT RED as required, Python fixed but Rust not yet (run against the 09:07
prebuilt cdcp_gate binary, stdout compared byte-for-byte):
  [prose]     DIFFERS  py=1 rs=0
  [readmepath]DIFFERS  py=1 rs=1
  [dup]       DIFFERS  py=1 rs=1
  [minsites]  DIFFERS  py=1 rs=0

AFTER — all three RED, both implementations byte-identical:
  hole 1 middle case  -> exit 1  "advertises 36 known-bad injections; the suites self-reported 7"
  hole 1 site dropped -> exit 1  "only 4 advertisement site(s) parsed in <path>; at least 5 are expected"
  hole 1 agreeing word ("seven") -> exit 0 (parses, does not false-positive)
  hole 2              -> exit 1  findings name "<path>/README_off.md:3"; zero findings say README.md
  hole 3              -> exit 1  "--require names 'spec_alpha' more than once ..."; no measured_total line
  hole 3 dangerous    -> exit 1

KNOWN-GOOD: live tree, receipts collected from a REAL run of all nine registered suites
(all rc=0) -> exit 0, measured_total=36, readme_claims=[36], byte-identical py/rust.
Anti-vacuous unchanged and re-verified: missing log / empty log / whitespace-only log all
exit 1 in both, stdout identical.

META-TEST PAIR (charter definition):
  leg 1  MUTATE the gate (duplicate --require guard disabled -> the double-count returns),
         cargo test --test diff_verify_injection_count -> TRUE EXIT 101, exactly one failure:
         a_suite_named_twice_in_require_is_identical_and_an_error
  leg 2  mutation STILL IN PLACE (verified by grep), delete that test -> TRUE EXIT 0, 30 passed.
         So the assertion is what caught it, not something else.
  restored -> TRUE EXIT 0, 31 passed.
  (A second mutation, MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES 5->4 in the Rust only, is caught by THREE
   independent assertions — stronger, but not a clean single-assertion pair.)

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2021 --check clean on both my .rs files; clippy -D warnings clean;
cargo test -p cdcp_gate fully green (all suites); cdcp_registry_check OK; tests/voice-slop.sh
exit 0; scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh exit 0 unchanged; repo_surface
no_overclaiming_language_in_the_shipped_surface ok. No new .py/.sh. Port still exits 1.

title: Three gates print PASS then crash — verdict emitted before a path that can still raise
description:
WHAT: Three gates print PASS (or most of a PASS report) to stdout and THEN die
with an uncaught exception. Make each fail closed BEFORE emitting a verdict.

WHY: A verdict followed by a crash is the worst possible output shape. A reader
skimming stdout sees PASS; CI sees non-zero; the two disagree, and which one wins
depends on whether anyone looked. Worse, any consumer that greps stdout for PASS
— including a human — gets the wrong answer from a gate that actually failed.
All three found 2026-08-14 by port agents, reproduced faithfully rather than
fixed, and pinned in the differential tests.

1. verify_doc_consistency.py — RAGGED ROW. `parse_doc` falls back to the
   heading's status when a data row has fewer cells than the Status column. If
   the heading is not itself a status word the fallback is None, the row is
   recorded with status=None and NO error, and main() then hits
       seen = ",".join(sorted({r["status"] for r in rows}))
   -> TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, NoneType found
   AFTER printing PASS and most of the summary. Trigger: `| M2 | ragged row |`
   under a non-status heading such as `## Notes on the waves`.
   OPEN DECISION for whoever fixes it: status=None should almost certainly be
   fail-closed ("row is shorter than its Status column") rather than rendered as
   the string None. That is a behaviour change, which is why it was not made.

2. verify_bank.py — ZERO EXAM SIZE. `exam_n_items = 0` silently falls back to 40
   because `or` treats 0 as falsy. `exam_n_items = "0"` instead reaches n/exam_n
   and raises ZeroDivisionError after printing three lines of a PASS report. Two
   spellings of the same value, two different wrong behaviours, neither an error.

3. verify_content_lock.py — two uncaught paths: the bank-hash subprocess exits 0
   with output that strips empty, so the oracle does [][-1] -> IndexError; and
   subprocess timeout=300 -> TimeoutExpired.

ALSO IN verify_bank.py, a latent nondeterminism worth fixing in the same pass:
`ALLOWED_CORRECT` is a frozenset and the diversity loop iterates it, so emission
order is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent. Harmless TODAY only because two letters cannot
both exceed 70% (they would sum past 140%), so at most one line is ever emitted.
Lower that threshold below 50% and the gate's output becomes nondeterministic
run to run — which would silently break every byte-exact differential test built
against it. The Rust ports iterate A-D and document why that is currently
equivalent.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch the corresponding
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs go RED, then change the port to match. Fixing
the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the differential test flags the
FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No gate emits PASS on stdout before a path that can still raise. Verdict is the
  LAST thing written, or it is not written.
- Known-bad per defect: ragged row -> RED naming the row; exam_n_items = "0" and
  = 0 -> both RED or both defaulted, consistently and stated; empty subprocess
  output -> ERROR not IndexError.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all fixes.
- ALLOWED_CORRECT iterated in a fixed order; a test pins the order.
- The diff_*.rs tests pinning each defect are DELETED (not amended) as each is
  fixed — the pin exists to make the repair deliberate, not permanent.
- Meta-test as the CHARTER now defines it: MUTATE the gate, confirm the suite
  trips, then delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm
  it passes. True exit codes, never read through a pipe.

title: content.lock gate has no tree-side walk — deleting a row silently stops checking that file
description:
WHAT: verify_content_lock.py has NO tree-side walk. It enumerates only rows
already in content.lock, so a file that is never listed is never checked, and
DELETING a row silently stops checking that file. Add a tree-side sweep, or
state the hole in the gate's own output rather than only in a header comment.

WHY: Confirmed empirically 2026-08-14 by the port agent, both directions:
  - Planted knowledge/smuggled_policy.toml and modules/99-smuggled.md. Both
    implementations exit 0 with `knowledge=9 modules=31` UNCHANGED.
  - Deleted the content.lock row for knowledge/claims.toml, then CORRUPTED that
    file. Both sides stayed GREEN. The only tell was the count moving to
    `knowledge=8` — a number nobody is asserting against anything.

The second direction is the dangerous one and it is the exact fooled-certificate
shape: the gate's coverage is defined by the artifact the gate is checking, so an
attacker (or an ordinary careless commit) removes coverage and the removal looks
identical to a pass. This is L7's content lock — the constellation.lock pattern —
whose entire purpose is "the pinned content still matches". A pin you can delete
without the gate noticing is not a pin.

Note the count IS emitted (`knowledge=9 modules=31`), so the information needed
to catch this is already on stdout. Nothing asserts against it. That is the
cheapest possible first fix: pin the expected counts, so a row deletion is RED.
The fuller fix is a tree-side walk with an explicit ignore list.

RELATED, same class, found the same day: scripts/verify_bank.py and
scripts/verify_knowledge_paths.py both have vacuity holes where zero-checked
reports identically to all-checked (see bd-...-jhd.5's report: a registry whose
every row is a licensed empty prints PASS / primary_notes_checked=0).

ACCEPTANCE:
- A file present under a locked root but absent from content.lock is RED, or the
  gate's OUTPUT states which roots it does not cover. A header comment is not
  sufficient — the reader of a green verdict must be told what it does not mean.
- Deleting a content.lock row is RED. Known-bad: delete the claims.toml row ->
  non-zero.
- Anti-vacuous: zero rows, or zero files discovered under a locked root, is an
  ERROR, never a pass.
- The two tests currently pinning these holes as agreed behaviour
  (`an_unlisted_file_slips_past_both_implementations`,
  `deleting_a_row_silently_stops_checking_that_file_in_both`) are DELETED in the
  same commit, because the behaviour they pin will no longer exist.
- Python first, then the port — the differential test must flag the port, not the fix.

title: cargo fmt cannot see src/gates/*.rs — audit which other tools stop at the #[path] boundary
description:
WHAT: `cargo fmt --check` cannot see crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs. Decide
whether the glob-based gate registration keeps its `#[path]` indirection (and
check.sh keeps the compensating per-file rustfmt leg added 2026-08-14), or
whether registration changes shape so cargo's own tooling reaches the files.

WHY: The gate modules are pulled in by `#[path = ...]` from a build.rs-generated
OUT_DIR file. `cargo fmt` walks the module tree from src/lib.rs and never
resolves that indirection, so it silently formats and checks NOTHING under
src/gates/.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, not inferred:
  - substrate_guard.rs deliberately misformatted -> `cargo fmt --check` exit 0,
    zero output. `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` on the same file -> exit 1,
    47-line diff.
  - Sweeping all nine gate files with rustfmt found THREE genuinely unformatted:
    install_hooks.rs, substrate_guard.rs, verify_orphans.rs. Two of those were
    already committed in 27a0c2d. They had never been checked by anything.
  - The five port agents that used per-file `rustfmt --check` were clean. The
    ones that relied on `cargo fmt` were not. The tool was the difference.

THIS IS THE COST OF THE PARALLELISM, AND THAT TRADE SHOULD BE MADE DELIBERATELY.
The glob registration is what lets N port agents each add exactly one file with
zero shared-file collisions — verified working under SIX concurrent agents, and
it is the reason 19 ports are parallelisable at all. It is worth keeping. But it
created an unchecked surface, and a green fmt leg over files it never opened is
the same vacuous-scan pattern check.sh hard-fails on everywhere else. The bug is
not that cargo fmt is wrong; it is that we adopted an indirection without
auditing which tools stop working across it.

MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED: check.sh now runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` per
file over the glob, with an anti-vacuous floor (zero gate files scanned = ERROR).
Proven to trip: misformatted gate -> exit 2 naming the file; empty glob -> exit 2.
That closes fmt specifically. This bead exists because fmt is unlikely to be the
only tool that cannot cross a `#[path]`/OUT_DIR boundary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Enumerate every tool in the chain that walks the module tree rather than the
  filesystem, and state for each whether it reaches src/gates/*.rs. At minimum:
  cargo fmt, clippy, rustdoc, cargo-mutants, tarpaulin/llvm-cov, cargo-udeps.
  `clippy --all-targets` is believed to reach them because it compiles; CONFIRM
  that by misformatting-equivalent injection, do not assume it.
- For each tool that does NOT reach them, either a compensating per-file leg with
  an anti-vacuous floor, or a recorded decision that the tool is not required.
- A meta-test per compensating leg: it trips on a known-bad file AND errors on an
  empty glob.
- If the decision is to change registration shape instead, the six-way-concurrent
  no-collision property must be preserved and re-demonstrated, not assumed.

title: SEV-0: guard reads paths from the index but the allowlist from the worktree — a commit is approved against a tree that never exists
description:
WHAT: The commit-time leg reads candidate paths from the git INDEX but reads
registries/substrate_allowlist.toml from the WORKING TREE. Read the allowlist
from the index too (`git show :registries/substrate_allowlist.toml`) whenever the
paths came from the index, so a commit is judged against the tree it creates.

WHY: CONFIRMED BY INJECTION 2026-08-14 (adversarial review, then reproduced by
the controller against a throwaway index):

    printf 'print("payload")\n' > scripts/payload.py
    git add scripts/payload.py
    # append a valid [[allow]] row for it, and do NOT git add the allowlist
    cdcp_gate substrate-guard            -> EXIT 0
    cdcp_gate substrate-guard --staged   -> EXIT 0

The resulting commit contains scripts/payload.py and does NOT contain the row
that authorised it. The guard approved a tree that has never existed and will
never exist. The next run on a clean checkout would flag the file — but the
commit is already in history, and in a public repo that is the part that matters.

The general shape, which is worth stating because it will recur: a gate that
mixes two sources of truth (index for the subject, worktree for the policy) is
judging a hybrid state that no commit ever has. Both halves must come from the
same snapshot.

RELATED, same root cause, same fix: the hook likewise evaluates the WORKTREE
copies of scripts/check.sh and the gate sources while committing possibly
neutered STAGED versions of them. So the BUILT != WIRED detector can read a
correctly-wired check.sh while the commit removes the wiring.

ACCEPTANCE:
- When candidates come from the index, the allowlist and check.sh are read from
  the index at the same revision. If a file is absent from the index, that is an
  ERROR (the commit deletes the policy), never a pass.
- Known-bad: the exact reproduction above -> exit 2 naming scripts/payload.py.
- Known-bad: stage a check.sh with the substrate-guard step deleted while the
  worktree copy still has it -> RED.
- Known-GOOD: staging the file AND its row together -> 0. This is the normal
  workflow and must not become harder.
- Anti-vacuous: an index with zero entries is an ERROR.
- Meta-test: mutate the index-reading path, confirm the suite trips; then delete
  the assertion with the mutation in place and confirm it passes.

title: SEV-0: wiring detector accepts inert shell — ': "cargo run ..."' and '|| true' both certify wired=yes
description:
WHAT: `check_sh_wires_guard()` decides "wired" by looking for a line containing
both "cdcp_gate" and the gate NAME, excluding comment/echo/ok lines. That admits
inert shell. Require evidence the step actually EXECUTES and that its failure
propagates.

WHY: CONFIRMED BY INJECTION 2026-08-14. Replacing the real call in check.sh with

    : "cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard"   # inert no-op

leaves the guard reporting `wired=yes` at exit 0. The `:` builtin does nothing.
These also certify:

    true # cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- substrate-guard || true      # failure swallowed

The last one is the nastiest: the gate genuinely runs, and its verdict is
discarded. "Wired" currently means "a string appears", not "a failure stops the
build" — which is the only property anyone cares about.

Two more holes in the same block:
- `[wiring].status` may be set back to "pending" after having been "wired". A
  gate that can be un-wired by editing one word is not ratcheted.
- `check_sh` is not pinned to scripts/check.sh. Point it at any file containing a
  suitable inert string and wiring is satisfied.

ACKNOWLEDGED DESIGN LIMIT: no substring test can prove a shell line executes.
The honest fix is not a better regex — it is to stop asking check.sh's TEXT and
start asking its BEHAVIOUR. Prefer: a selftest that runs check.sh against a
planted unlisted .py and asserts check.sh itself exits non-zero. That is a
behavioural assertion and it cannot be satisfied by an inert line.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Wiring is established by RUNNING check.sh against a planted known-bad and
  observing a non-zero exit, not by scanning its text.
- Known-bad: each of the three inert forms above -> RED.
- Known-bad: `[wiring].status` moved "wired" -> "pending" while the step is
  absent -> RED (ratchet, not a toggle).
- Known-bad: check_sh pointed at a file other than scripts/check.sh -> ERROR.
- Known-GOOD: the real check.sh -> 0.
- Meta-test: mutate the behavioural assertion, confirm the suite trips.

title: Substrate floor is a filename policy on one commit path — .PY, shebang-only, docs/, merge/rebase/cherry-pick, commit-tree, fresh clones all bypass
description:
WHAT: The substrate floor is a FILENAME policy, not a "non-Rust source" policy,
and pre-commit is not the only way a commit is created. Decide the real scope and
close the gaps, or state the narrowed claim everywhere the broad one is written.

WHY: adversarial review 2026-08-14, every item below confirmed by injection.

SCOPE GAPS (all returned exit 0 while staged):
    scripts/payload.PY          uppercase extension
    scripts/payload             no extension, `#!/usr/bin/env python3`
    scripts/payload.bash        another shell extension
    docs/payload.py             outside scan.roots
Also already outside the floor at 27a0c2d, four real shell files:
    .flywheel/scripts/publishability-bar.sh · .flywheel/watchdog.sh
    tests/publishability-bar.sh · tests/voice-slop.sh
A directory symlink or submodule is opaque the same way — git reports the link,
not the .py files beneath it.

COMMIT-PATH GAPS: only `pre-commit` is installed. Git runs different hooks for
merge (`pre-merge-commit`), rebase (`pre-rebase`), and `git am`
(`pre-applypatch`), and the sequencer does not fire `pre-commit` for ordinary
cherry-pick/rebase commits. Plumbing bypasses hooks entirely:
    git commit-tree $(git write-tree) -p HEAD -m payload
`core.hooksPath=/dev/null` redirects hook lookup away from the installed shim.
And hooks are NEVER CLONED: a fresh clone has no hook at all, the committed shim
is mode 100644, and nothing installs it before the first ordinary commit. The CI
workflow checks out fresh and runs check.sh but never runs install-hooks — so
`install-hooks --check` should be RED in CI today.

IT ALSO DOES NOT FAIL `cargo build`. Neither `cargo build --workspace` nor
`cargo test --workspace` runs the repository presence scan; only check.sh does.
"Fails the build" is therefore true only of one shell orchestrator.

THE HONEST FRAMING, which is the real deliverable here: this gate raises the cost
of CASUALLY adding a .py/.sh through the ordinary `git commit` path in a clone
where the hook is installed. It is not, and given hooks-are-advisory cannot be, a
containment boundary against someone who does not want to be stopped. Server-side
enforcement (a CI job on the pushed ref, or a pre-receive hook) is the only place
a real boundary can live. Say that in the header instead of implying more.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision on scope: extensions case-insensitive? shebang sniffing?
  roots = whole repo minus an ignore list? Each choice recorded with its reason.
- Whatever is decided, a known-bad per bypass class that currently passes.
- CI runs `install-hooks` (or the equivalent) so a fresh clone is guarded, and
  `install-hooks --check` is green in CI rather than vacuously unrun.
- A server-side check on the pushed ref, or a written decision that we accept
  client-side-only and why.
- The gate header and every commit message stop saying "fails the build and is
  refused at commit" and say what is actually enforced, where.

title: smoke_diagrams: a registry row can point at the registry itself — deriving fixed WHICH items, not HOW they are checked
description:
WHAT: smoke_diagrams' registry-derived check selects rows by regex and then
trusts whatever path the row names. Bind the row to the artifact.

WHY: confirmed by injection 2026-08-14, after the derive-from-registry fix that
was itself meant to close a hardcoding hole. Point a row at the registry document
itself:

  | `fire-sequence` | ... | P1 | **present** | `docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md` |

The file exists, and it contains the substrings "not", "certif", and
"fire-sequence" — so every predicate passes and web/diagrams/fire-sequence.html
is never opened. Measured: exit 0, "PASS (7 present diagrams from the registry)".

Three more, same shape:
- Status spelled `shipped` instead of `**present**` silently drops that one row
  while the other six keep the zero-row anti-vacuous error from firing. Partial
  coverage loss reports identically to full coverage.
- Removing the backticks from a row's ID or path makes the regex skip it.
- The whole "diagram" `not certif fire-sequence` passes every content predicate.

THE LESSON, and the reason this bead is worth reading: deriving the list from a
registry fixed WHICH ITEMS get checked and left HOW they are checked untouched.
The registry became a new place to write the same lie. Deriving is necessary and
not sufficient — the derived reference has to be BOUND to the artifact.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A row's path must live under web/diagrams/ and its basename must match its ID.
- The expected count is pinned, so a row silently leaving the PRESENT set is RED
  rather than invisible.
- Content predicates are structural, not substring: parse for the honesty banner
  element and the data-diagram attribute rather than grepping for "not"/"certif".
- Known-bad per bypass above -> RED, including the status-typo case.
- Known-GOOD: the live 7 -> 0.
- Anti-vacuous stays: zero present rows, and an unreadable registry, are ERROR.

title: Hub mastery catalog is pinned at 14 — module 15 is taught and assessed but cannot appear in learner progress
description:
WHAT: web/assets/js/hub_mastery.js MODULE_CATALOG holds 14 slugs, ending at
14-auxiliary. Module 15 is absent, so the hub mastery surface cannot show it.
Derive the catalog from the same registry the Learn index uses, and rebase
scripts/smoke_hub_mastery.mjs off the derived count.

WHY: C5 closed the fairness defect — module 15 was ASSESSED but never TAUGHT —
by shipping web/learn/15-ops-adjacent.html (7,211 words) and 39 approved items.
That part is real and holds. But the PRODUCT-FACING leg was missed: MODULE_CATALOG
drives the mastery/progress surface rendered on web/index.html and web/learn.html,
and it stops at 14. A learner is assessed on module 15, can read module 15, and
cannot see their module-15 progress anywhere.

CONTROLLER ERROR, recorded so it is not repeated: I closed
bd-hardening-c-status-hzs.4 grading it "acceptance fully met", citing the report
line "Learn hub lists 15 modules, not 14". web/learn/ does contain 15 HTML files,
so the sentence was true — but the mastery CATALOG is a different artifact and it
was never checked. This is the second time on this same bead that I measured the
wrong file: I also first counted the Learn page's HTML shell (131 words) instead
of its content markdown (7,211). Verifying a claim means finding the artifact the
claim is about, not the nearest artifact with a matching name.

THIRD INSTANCE TODAY OF THE bd-lt7 PATTERN, and the reason this bead is P1 rather
than P2: scripts/smoke_hub_mastery.mjs:77 asserts
    assert(MODULE_CATALOG.length === 14, "MODULE_CATALOG has 14 modules");
plus two `m <= 14` sweep loops. So ADDING module 15 to the catalog FAILS THE GATE.
The gate layer has written the defect down as a requirement again — after
smoke_learn/smoke_feedback_links/smoke_weak_links did exactly this for the same
module, and after the smoke_diagrams per-item exemption for power-path did it one
layer down. A fixer without this context reads the red gate as a reason to revert.

ACCEPTANCE:
- MODULE_CATALOG is DERIVED from knowledge/domains.toml (or the same
  modules_index.json build_units.py now uses) — not a hand-maintained literal.
- smoke_hub_mastery.mjs asserts the catalog matches the derived registry count,
  never a numeric literal. Its two `m <= 14` sweeps follow the derived length.
- Known-bad: a module declared in the registry but absent from the catalog -> RED
  naming the module. This is the leg that would have caught C5's product side.
- Known-GOOD: the live tree with 15 modules passes; a legitimate 14-module tree
  would also pass, so the fix is not "change 14 to 15".
- Anti-vacuous: an empty catalog, or zero modules discovered, is an ERROR.
- Meta-test per the CHARTER: MUTATE the derivation, confirm the suite trips; then
  with the mutation still in place delete the assertion and confirm it passes.
- crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs open-instance count drops from 5
  as each is closed; it must never grow silently.
